title: ‘Friday Night Lights,’ ‘Mosquito Bowl’ author says America has lost the Greatest Generation's sense of duty
summary: "The Mosquito Bowl" author Buzz Bissinger says America has forgotten the selfless duty of the Greatest Generation, whose college football stars left fame behind to fight in WWII.
story: "Friday Night Lights" and "The Mosquito Bowl" author Buzz Bissinger tells Fox News Digital why modern America must remember the ordinary men who sacrificed everything during World War II.
"Friday Night Lights" author Buzz Bissinger believes modern America has lost touch with the selflessness that once defined the "Greatest Generation."

The 72-year-old Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist penned the 2022 nonfiction book "The Mosquito Bowl," which was adapted into Peter Berg's new Netflix war movie of the same name. "The Mosquito Bowl" tells the true story of elite college football stars who walked away from fame and future wealth to enlist in the Marines and fight in the Pacific Theater during World War II.
While speaking with Fox News Digital at the film's premiere during the AFI Film Festival, Bissinger argued that kind of sacrifice has largely disappeared today.
HOLLYWOOD MARINE VETERAN ROB RIGGLE DOUBTS MODERN STARS WOULD MAKE JIMMY STEWART'S WWII SACRIFICE

"I think we've forgotten," Bissinger said. "I know they're called the Greatest Generation, but we have forgotten what it is like to serve, to have a sense of duty, to do something regardless of whether you're going to come back or not. And these are things we have to remember."

"Friday Night Lights" and "The Mosquito Bowl" author Buzz Bissinger believes that modern America has lost the sense of duty that defined the Greatest Generation.  (Brianna Bryson/FilmMagic; Circa Images/GHI/Universal History Archive/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

"We were together," he continued. "These men fought. They were never heroes. They never thought of themselves as heroes. They were ordinary men in extraordinary circumstances who felt it was really, really important to serve their country. And many of them didn't come back."
AMERICA'S VETERANS AND MILITARY HEROES DESERVE FAR MORE RECOGNITION THAN THEY GET: YOUTUBE STAR

"And they need to be memorialized," he added. "It helps remind me of the greatness of this country, just how great this country was. There was no division. We were in unison, and these men personified that. And they had great lives ahead of them, but they didn't make it."

Both the book and the movie depict the Mosquito Bowl, a tackle football game played on Christmas Eve in 1944 on Guadalcanal between two Marine regiments whose ranks included some of the country's top former college football players. Months later, 15 of the 65 players were killed fighting in the Battle of Okinawa.
WATCH: 'Friday Night Lights' author Buzz Bissinger says America has 'forgotten' the Greatest Generation's duty
FOX SPORTS TO HONOR MILITARY AHEAD OF VETERANS DAY WITH TWO-DAY SALUTE DURING COLLEGE FOOTBALL, NFL COVERAGE

During his interview with Fox News Digital, Bissinger drew a comparison between modern celebrity sports culture and the dozens of elite college athletes who put their lives on the line in World War II, many of whom had already been drafted by NFL teams.

"I was actually thinking about how many pro football players have served in the military. The answer is virtually none," he said. "To have 65 football players who went to college and are now in the Marine Corps serving, forget it."
KELSEY GRAMMER STILL FEELS 'SENSE OF SMALLNESS' FOR NOT SERVING IN MILITARY: 'I DO MY BEST TO MAKE UP FOR IT'
"It was a whole different era," Bissinger continued. "You gave up your dreams. You had no choice. You had to serve. It was in your heart."
Bissinger said that the Marines who fought in WWII "personified" the country's unity.  (Getty Images)

He cited Dave Schreiner, a celebrated University of Wisconsin two-time All-American football star who turned down an NFL career and non-combat military posts to enlist in the U.S. Marine Corps and serve on the front lines.
Schreiner was mortally wounded during the Battle of Okinawa in June 1945 and died the following day at age 24.
LAST SURVIVING 'ROSIE THE RIVETERS' HONORED BY WWII MUSEUM ON D-DAY ANNIVERSARY: 'WE CAN DO IT'

"All of them could have gotten out, I think, because they were athletes, and athletes are coveted," Bissinger said. "But they didn't. They didn't. It was offered, and they said, ‘No, I have to go. I have to go.’ And that's pretty rare. You will not see that happen today."
The author said the Marines featured in his book were "ordinary men in extraordinary circumstances." (Getty Images)
Bissinger pointed out that many of the football players who fought in WWII could have used their status to get safer stateside opportunities but refused.
THE DAY AFTER MEMORIAL DAY, AMERICA’S DEBT TO THE FALLEN STILL REMAINS

Berg's adaptation of "The Mosquito Bowl" focuses on four real-life college football stars who enlisted in the Marines after Pearl Harbor, including Schreiner, who was played by Broadway star Tom Francis, John McLaughry (Nicholas Galitzine), Bob Baumann (Bill Skarsgård) and Tony Butkovich (Ray Nicholson). The screenplay was co-written by Berg and Mark L Smith.
PETER BERG SAYS 'CALL OF DUTY' MOVIE WILL EXPLORE 'THE COST OF WAR' WITH SERIOUS TONE

Bissinger spent five years researching and writing "The Mosquito Bowl" including digging through military records and family archives. While speaking with Fox News Digital, the author compared the process to a "detective story" since many of the first-hand witnesses and people who participated in the real-life Mosquito Bowl had died.
During his research, Bissinger made a personal discovery when he unexpectedly uncovered his own late father's service in the 4th Marine Regiment.
Bissinger spent five years researching and writing "The Mosquito Bowl." (Gamma-Keystone via Getty Images)
"He never talked about it. I didn't know, was he on the line? Was he a rifleman? Was he, you know, a waiter?" Bissinger recalled.
Bissinger, who was born Harry Gerard Bissinger III, explained that he was searching for his own name in the records since he was named after his father.

"So I looked up the roster records, and his name is my name," Bissinger said. "I'm the third, he's the second. And there's his name. But not only that, he is a rifleman, so he's on the lines. And he's in the 4th Regiment, which is one of the regiments that I was writing about, so I'm seeing all these names from the book and, for all I know, he could have been there. He could have been at the game."

"It was mind-blowing, and it put me over the top," he continued. "And what I learned — I'm so proud of him. And I stop because I get worked up. I just wish I could have said that 'I'm really proud of you. I'm really, really proud of you.' But he's been gone for a long time."
However, Bissinger told Fox News Digital that learning about his father's history established a connection that they didn't have when he was alive.
"I've never felt closer to him," Bissinger said.

The Pacific Theater of World War II officially ended on September 2, 1945 (V-J Day), when Japanese representatives signed the formal Instrument of Surrender aboard the battleship USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay. (Universal History Archive/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

Berg's late father, Laurence Berg, was also a Marine who served in the Korean War. Bissinger recalled he and the director, who are also second cousins, recently shared a moment in which they wondered how their fathers would have reacted to "The Mosquito Bowl."
"Last week, we were walking out of the Marine Corps Museum, and we both said, ‘What would it be like if our fathers were here?,'" Bissinger said.

"Now, they were kind of critical guys, so the first thing they would do is criticize the film, but then they would hug us, and they would feel such incredible pride, not just for us, but for the family," he continued. "It would have been a great moment, but we'll have to imagine it."
"The Mosquito Bowl" stars Ray Nicholson as Tony Butkovich, Tom Francis as Dave Schreiner, Bill Skarsgård as Bob Baumann, and Nicholas Galitzine as John McLaughry.  (Kane Skennar / Netflix )

Bissinger said that while audiences remain hungry for stories about real-life heroes like his father and the men of the Mosquito Bowl, he believes Hollywood too often waters down the true cost of combat.

"I think what happens is, particularly in war movies, they ultimately get sanitized," he said. "Filmmakers, directors, studios are afraid of showing war as it is because they think people can't handle it. I think that's ridiculous, and I think it's wrong."

"In order for us to see just how tragic and brutal war is, we have to see it," Bissinger continued. "We have to see it. I tried to do that in the book and Pete has certainly done that in the film. People may flinch, people may not be able to handle it, but to me, it doesn't matter. If you want to know what war is like, you have to watch this film and read other books, and maybe, maybe collectively, we'll say, ‘Enough.’"
WATCH: 'Friday Night Lights' author Buzz Bissinger says 'The Mosquito Bowl' cast nailed it 'to a T'
Bissinger told Fox News Digital that he keeps a picture of Schreiner hanging on his wall to remind him of the harsh realities of war and the sacrifices made by the fallen players.

"I still can't quite comprehend that these guys are no longer with us," he said. "Dave Schreiner, beautiful guy, 6'2", perfect, the perfect two-time All-American, great son, great family, and his whole life ahead of him. And he died 12 hours before officials surrendered."

"And I'm just haunted by that," Bissinger continued. "Because he should have — they should have had a life. They didn't waste their lives, but it's still, in a sense, is the waste of a good human being. And that's just hard for me to overcome. So he reminds me, he keeps me going."
Bissinger said he keeps a picture of Schreiner hanging on his wall.  (Kane Skennar / Netflix )
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Bissinger admitted that ahead of watching "The Mosquito Bowl," he was worried about whether the film and its young cast would preserve the integrity of the men they were portraying. However, he told Fox News Digital that he was blown away by their performances.

"They did it to a T," he said. "They're all great. Ray Nicholson will knock your socks off. Bill Skarsgård, Tom Francis, Nick Galitzine — they were phenomenal. And so at a certain point, I'm not looking at them as people they're making a movie about, I am seeing them now as the characters they were, and that was great."

"The Mosquito Bowl" marks a creative reunion for Bissinger and Berg. The director previously adapted Bissinger's 1990 bestselling nonfiction book "Friday Night Lights" into the acclaimed 2004 movie of the same name and later the hit TV series that ran on NBC from 2006 to 2011.
Bissinger praised the young cast, saying, they "did it to a T." (Kane Skennar / Netflix )
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Bissinger also credited Berg, who is known for helming gritty, realistic filmmaking after having helmed "Lone Survivor," "Deepwater Horizon" and "Patriots Day," with refusing to compromise the book's spirit.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"He, to a T, wants to retain authenticity and the integrity of the book and he did that in ‘Friday Night Lights’ and since then we've really become brothers," Bissinger said. "We talk all the time. I pitch projects to him. He says, 'You're out of your mind. I'm not doing that.' But then something hits and it took a while. It took a little while."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"But once he got the thread, which is really about the loss of innocence, he got it," he said. "He's fun to work with. He is a hoot on the set. He has a great character. Hollywood needs more of them, I'll tell you."

title: British police name suspects charged in break-in at Prince William and Princess Kate's home
summary: Two men are charged after a break-in at Prince William and Princess Kate's Anmer Hall on the Sandringham Estate, with police deploying dogs and drones.
story: Royal reporter Kinsey Schofield discusses how two people were able to break into a cottage belonging to the UK’s royal family on ‘Fox News @ Night.’
British police announced on Wednesday two men have been charged following a report of a break-in at Prince William and Princess Kate’s country home on the Sandringham Estate.
The Norfolk Constabulary confirmed that Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, were arrested in connection with the incident at Anmer Hall; authorities said the property was unoccupied at the time.
The men have been charged with entering a dwelling with intent to steal and trespassing on a protected site. They remain in custody and are due to appear in Norwich Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday.
The suspects were taken into custody near the country house after police received a call about suspicious activity at around 6 p.m. local time (1 p.m. ET) on Monday.

British police are seen on Nov. 24, 2026, at the royal family’s Sandringham Estate investigating a burglary at Anmer Hall, a secondary residence of Prince William and Princess Kate. (Martin Pope/Getty Images)
FORMER PRINCE ANDREW ‘SHAKEN’ BY MASKED MAN THREAT, BUT MORE SECURITY WOULD SPARK ‘PUBLIC BACKLASH’: EXPERT

"Officers attended and specialist resources, including police dogs, drones and the National Police Air Service helicopter, were deployed to assist with searches in the area," police said in a statement to Fox News.

The Sun reported that William, Kate, and their three children — Prince George, Princess Charlotte, and Prince Louis — were staying at their primary residence, Forest Lodge in Windsor, at the time of the incident.
Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom residence on the 20,000-acre Sandringham Estate, was given to William and Kate as a wedding gift by the late Queen Elizabeth II.

Prior to moving in, the couple oversaw a £1.5 million renovation that included major security upgrades, such as rerouting a public road, planting dense tree lines for privacy and establishing a seasonal no-fly zone over the property.

Prince William, Prince of Wales, Duke of Rothesay, and Catherine, Princess of Wales, Duchess of Rothsay, with Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis arrive for the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games at The Hydro on Aug. 1, 2026 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Jeff J. Mitchell/Getty Images)
RENTALS NOW ALLOWED IN HISTORIC WATER TOWER ON KING CHARLES' SANDRINGHAM ESTATE WHERE ROYALS SPEND CHRISTMAS
The family regularly visits the country estate for weekend getaways and school holidays, and it served as a private sanctuary for Kate during her cancer treatment in 2024.
The break-in raises fresh concerns over royal security, as William and his immediate family receive 24-hour armed protection as working royals.
The incident also marks the latest security scare on royal grounds.
A general view of the front of Anmer Hall on the Sandringham Estate on Jan. 13, 2013 in King's Lynn, England. (Indigo/Getty Images)

In 2024, two masked burglars broke into Shaw Farm on the Windsor Castle Estate while William, Kate and their children were sleeping nearby at Adelaide Cottage.
In May, a man was arrested following an incident at Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor’s residence on the Sandringham Estate, The Sun reported.

title: ‘The Vow’ star Jace Cates recommits to saving himself for marriage despite ‘sex-positive culture’
summary: "Chris Harrison’s: The Vow" star Jace Cates opens up about saving himself for marriage, why faith in relationships matters, and dating in a sex-positive culture.
story: The reality star is committed to waiting until marriage to be intimate with someone again, going against today's "sex-positive culture."
"Chris Harrison's: The Vow" star, Jace Cates, is giving his opinion on modern dating and how the current "sex-positive culture" can complicate things.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 30-year-old reality star said he is committed to saving himself for marriage, noting that while he was in his 20s, "there were times that I absolutely" wasn't in "lockstep with my faith," noting that might be why he was "single at 30."

"I talk about being a fan of Jesus or also being a follower of Jesus. There's a big difference," he said. "So, when you're a follower of Jesus, there is specific beliefs that you have to actually be a follower of Jesus to build that relationship around Jesus and have faith be a part of the relationship. And the next person I'm intimate with, I want that to be my wife. And I think that's important."
Adding: "And I know it's hard, because it's a very sex-positive culture. And it's a sacrifice for sure for people to make. And I think that's something that people have to navigate."
Jace Cates, 30, is searching for his future wife among 10 women on Fox Nation's faith-focused dating series "Chris Harrison's: The Vow." (Fox Nation)
CHRIS HARRISON RETURNS TO REALITY TV WITH 'THE VOW,' FOX NATION'S FIRST-EVER DATING SHOW

"I think we got away from being okay with talking about faith in a relationship and going to church together," he said. "And I think as people are looking intentionally and leading with faith, those are conversations that couples need to have sooner rather than later. That's about intentional dating and I think it's something that people need to discuss."
WATCH HERE: ‘CHRIS HARRISON’S: THE VOW'S' JACE CATES WANTS THE NEXT PERSON HE IS INTIMATE WITH TO BE HIS WIFE
The new Fox Nation show, "Chris Harrison's: The Vow," follows Cates as he navigates relationships with 10 women seeking lasting commitment and marriage over six episodes.
While on "Chris Harrison’s: The Vow," Cates navigates relationships with 10 women as he tries to find lasting love. (Fox Nation)
His experience on the show ultimately changed his view on dating, as he was left completely unplugged as he "was away from my phone, my laptop [and] couldn't communicate with my family."
WATCH HERE: JACE CATES SAYS BEING ‘UNPLUGGED’ WHILE FILMING ‘CHRIS HARRISON’S: THE VOW' HELPED HIM CONNECT WITH HIS FAITH

"All I could do was be in silence and rely on my relationship with God. And it's something I've tried to take back to my real life," he explained. "One thing I'll say, viewers, when they tune into the show and see what happens, I'm just extremely grateful that I had this experience to show me how important that is more than I even believed before I went on the show."
Case notes that technology also makes modern-day relationships more difficult. (Fox Nation)

In addition to the "sex-positive culture," Cates thinks technology is also a problem when it comes to modern dating, as "people have access to people now, more than ever," noting this is when being intentional in the pursuit of love is important.

Cates told Fox News Digital, that the faith aspect of the show separates it from others of its kind, noting everyone who participated was "trying to build something real and people actually looking for love."
Cates said he would like a traditional marriage in which they support one another 100%. (Fox Nation)

When it comes to what he is looking for in a relationship, the Oregon native admitted he is hoping for a more traditional marriage, but not in the way people might think, noting the term has a "negative connotation right now."

"I think for me, traditional marriage means just supporting your person 100 percent in what they are looking to do in life," he said. "And if my future wife wants to be a stay-at-home mom, I want to be a supportive husband and support her 100 percent. If she wants to be a CEO of a company, I will support her 100 percent and we will make it work. I think that is what traditional means to me. And that's just because that's how my parents were in their relationship."

He also feels that the work at home should be split evenly when it comes to raising children, saying when he was growing up, both his mom and dad were very involved in his childhood, adding, "I just want to give that to my kids when I raise them, because it worked so well for me."
WATCH HERE: ‘CHRIS HARRISON’S: THE VOW' STAR DESCRIBED HIS VERSION OF A TRADITIONAL MARRIAGE

"I think men, you understand if you are gonna bring kids into this world, it is one of the most important jobs you're gonna have is to be a great father," he said. "I can only speak for men. You have responsibility, and it's time for you to step up and if you're not ready for it, then maybe that's not for you. title: Thomas Markle, estranged father of Meghan Markle, indicted on child pornography charges
summary: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, has been indicted on child pornography charges involving 35mm film negatives of minors under 12.
story: Meghan Markle's estranged father, Thomas Wayne Markle, is deemed mentally competent to stand trial during a federal court hearing. He’s charged with one count of possession of child pornography.
Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, was indicted on child pornography charges.
Markle, 82, is charged with possessing child sexual abuse material (CSAM), specifically 35 mm film negatives of prepubescent minors and minors who had not yet reached the age of 12 years old.
He remains jailed in Florida after he allegedly cut off his ankle monitor earlier this month. If convicted, Markle would face a statutory maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison on each count.
MEGHAN MARKLE COULD BE DRAGGED INTO FATHER'S CHILD SEX ABUSE CASE, EXPERT WARNS

Thomas Markle Sr. was arrested Nov. 10 and ordered to remain in custody after allegedly cutting off an ankle monitor that was a part of his conditional release on charges of possessing child sexual abuse material.  (Pinellas County Sheriff's Office)

On Oct. 30 and Nov. 4, Markle knowingly possessed 35 mm negatives that contained CSAM that had been mailed, shipped, and transported using any means and facility of interstate and foreign commerce, according to an indictment released Tuesday.

"During both instances, Markle knew the images were CSAM and at least one of the images involved a prepubescent minor and a minor who had not yet attained the age of 12 years old," according to a release provided by The United States Attorney's Office for the Central District of California.
THOMAS MARKLE ALLEGEDLY CUT OFF ANKLE MONITOR AFTER CHILD SEXUAL ABUSE MATERIAL ARREST

"Court documents in this case filed earlier this month allege that Markle knowingly possessed CSAM in the Philippines and at two rented storage facilities in Los Angeles. Pursuant to judicially authorized warrants, FBI special agents searched the two storage units registered to Markle. Markle has rented both storage units since 2008."
Thomas Markle Sr. was found to be mentally competent to stand trial last month at the Sam M. Gibbons United States Courthouse court in Tampa, Fla. (Douglas Land)

"Inside the units, agents seized approximately 78 items, including slides, film negatives, and books that contained suspected CSAM," officials added. "Two images depict an adult man – whom a witness identified as Markle – with a nude prepubescent girl. The third image depicts a nude prepubescent girl in a room that appears to be part of a motel chain in the Philippines. The affidavit also describes additional photographs that appear to show Markle with children in various stages of undress."
The FBI is investigating the matter.
Federal prosecutors charged Markle with one count of possessing child sexual abuse material in a criminal complaint filed Nov. 5 before he was arrested in Florida.

According to the 14-page complaint obtained by Fox News Digital, FBI agents searched two storage units registered to Markle and seized approximately 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books containing suspected child sexual abuse material. Investigators say Markle had rented the units since 2008 and continued paying for them through October 2026.
Meghan Markle condemned the alleged abuse in October. (Chris Jackson - Pool/Getty Images/Good Morning Britain/YouTube)

A witness, who had known Markle since the 1970s, allegedly identified him as the adult man appearing with a prepubescent girl in at least two photographs. The complaint did not name the witness.

The investigation began after Markle Sr.'s son, Thomas Markle Jr., reported finding storage boxes containing suspected child sexual abuse images at his father's local residence and turned the materials over to authorities.

"I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed," she said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital at the time.

"I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications' distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them," she wrote. title: Country singer Drake White admits he still fears another stroke seven years after nearly dying
summary: Drake White reveals the fear of another stroke lingers seven years after his hemorrhagic stroke, and how faith and Navy SEALs help him cope.
story: The 42-year-old country music star suffered a stroke that left his left side paralyzed
Seven years after suffering a hemorrhagic stroke that nearly killed him in 2019, country music star Drake White admits he still lives with the lingering fear of suffering another medical emergency.

Speaking exclusively to Fox News Digital at the third-annual Benefit For The Brain event in Nashville, the 43-year-old singer opened up about the lasting physical and mental toll of his health battle — and how he has learned to channel that anxiety into purpose.

"The fear of having another stroke is always there," White said. "Once your nervous system goes through that, it’s imprinted on it. You can work yourself into a tizzy, you can work yourself into anxiety attacks, and your heart rate gets up, your blood pressure gets going. So, it's about learning how to deal with that and breathe through it."
COUNTRY SINGER DRAKE WHITE DESCRIBES ‘GUNSHOT’ MOMENT HIS BRAIN RUPTURED MID-CONCERT: ‘I KNEW I WAS DYING’
Drake White attended a benefit for the brain at Ryman Auditorium in Nashville, Tenn., on Nov. 16, 2026. (Getty Images)

White credited both his background as an athlete and the support of friends — including several Navy SEALs in attendance at the benefit — with teaching him how to manage anxiety and high-stress situations.

"Just being confident in people saying, 'Hey, you're helping, keep going,'" he explained. "Because there are so many days that I don't want to keep going. So yeah, I fear sometimes, but there's a lot of good things in fear, too. You pay attention when you're scared."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Even seven years later, the memory of his near-death experience remains vivid.

"It feels just as real today," White said. "For me, I had a real-life experience where I witnessed a near-death experience. To come through that — that'll never leave me. I'm 43 now; I was 35 when that happened. So for me, it's very, very palpable. Very, very real."
Alex White and Drake White attended Drake White's benefit for the brain at Ryman Auditorium in Nashville, Tenn., on Nov. 16, 2026. (Getty Images)

"The thing is, God meets you where you're at," he added. "I don't care who you are, what you believe or what you think, if you cry out to Jesus, you cry out to God ... God's gonna meet you where you're at, and He's gonna come to you. And that's what happened. It was as clear as that."
In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital earlier this year, White reflected further on that life-changing moment and how leaning on his faith carried him through recovery.
CAN FAITH HELP PATIENTS HEAL? VETERAN DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT HE'S WITNESSED FIRSTHAND

Before hitting the road with Zac Brown in 2019, White was diagnosed with a rare brain condition called arteriovenous malformation (AVM). Having already undergone four surgeries, White said doctors told him the chance of a rupture was less than 1%. He decided to take the risk and continue touring.
His worst nightmare unfolded while doing what he loved most: performing.
REALITY STAR DR PIMPLE POPPER SUFFERED A STROKE WHILE FILMING HER SHOW, SAYS PART OF HER BRAIN 'DIED'
Drake White performs at his benefit for the brain at Ryman Auditorium on Nov. 16, 2026, in Nashville, Tenn. (Getty Images)

"We just took the stage in Roanoke, Virginia. It was probably 98 degrees and cotton candy skies, beautiful, 2,500 people out there. And I tore into three or four songs and I just felt a tick," White recalled. "I felt my left arm, my fingers tingling, kind of numbness. And then I heard what I call a gunshot. It literally sounded like an audible gunshot behind my left ear. And when it snapped, if you look at the video back, you can see me trying to push through it."

"I grew up in Alabama where you just kind of keep pushing, keep going, and I tried to do that, and I couldn't speak," he continued. "I couldn't think, and the cotton candy sky became the grass, and the grass became the sky. Everything flipped upside down ... Everything slowed way down, and it just felt like I was walking in quicksand, and everything was heavy. My left arm was heavy, my left foot was heavy, and I knew right then, I was like, 'Well, dang, I'm having a stroke.'"
White immediately remembered his doctors' warnings about what would happen if the AVM ruptured.

"They told me, 'If it ruptures, you would have a very good chance of death,'" he said. "Death was kind of it. And so I just remember thinking: Keep breathing, keep praying, and get me to the hospital."
RUDY GIULIANI REVEALS HE HAD 'SPIRITUAL EXPERIENCE' WHILE IN PNEUMONIA-RELATED COMA
White was rushed to a local hospital and administered a coagulant that stopped the brain bleed.
Drake was mid-performance during his 2019 stroke. (Jo Hale/Redferns)

"That ultimately saved my life, but in that process, [I] saw angels, had the whole near-death experience, talked to God, the whole thing," he said. "It humbled me down to my knees. I realized that rock bottom had a basement. It really got me to a spot where I didn't know if I was gonna survive."
At the time, the country singer was left paralyzed on his left side and uncertain of his future.

"That was when the mental battle started," White said. "The doctors came in and told me that I'd had a hemorrhagic stroke and that I had a long road ahead of me. They didn't say this directly, but I heard them murmuring that I'd be lucky to walk again, much less get back on stage."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"That's when my world kind of crashed in around me," he added. "I was thinking, 'I've put so much time into this, and I've been so passionate about it. What am I going to do now? I've got a bedpan and I can't even feed myself.'"
Amid his recovery, White and his wife, Alex, were hit with another tragedy six years after his stroke.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
In September 2025, the couple — who are parents to a 3-year-old son — announced the death of their newborn daughter, Della Elizabeth.
During this time, White leaned heavily on his family, friends and faith. Looking back, he describes his previous interaction with God during his near-death experience as "very peaceful."
Drake White credits his faith to pushing through tough times. (Danielle Del Valle/Getty Images)

"My faith, I like to describe it like this: The sun feels different on my cheek than it does on your cheek," he said. "I am a Jesus-following guy that believes in that wholeheartedly. Met Him, saw Him, talked to Him. It's as real as me and you talking right now ... He was like, 'What's going on? Tell me what's up. ' It was the most peaceful I'd ever been in my life in that moment."

"I was not scared," he continued. "It's just like a transition. I could feel it. It was palpable. You know what I mean? I could touch it ... Whatever faith is for you, it meets you where you are. It meets you where you are in a hospital bed or in a car wreck or whatever it is. It met me where I was."

Now, White is turning his new perspective into action through his Benefit For The Brain concert. Following two consecutive sold-out shows, the event’s third installment once again united major musical talent and passionate advocates to raise awareness and funds for brain and mental health.
For White, hosting the event is the fulfillment of a vow he made while fighting for his life.
Drake White performs at his benefit for the brain at Ryman Auditorium in Nashville, Tenn., on Nov. 16, 2026. (Getty Images)

"For me, it was just a promise to myself and a promise to God that if He let me out of the hospital — if He would get me to a place where I could live again — that I would help give back to people and show people how I got from the darkness to the light," White said.

"That promise was just something I could drive towards," he continued. "If you have a purpose, and you find that purpose and push towards it, then your life starts to make sense. None of that stuff made sense to me when I was going through it — there were a lot of whines and a lot of howls. But when you start seeing other people come up and say, 'Hey, you helped me through this,' or 'You helped me through cancer,' or 'You helped me through losing my son or daughter' — who am I to even be complaining about what I had to go through if I get an opportunity to help people? "

title: Intruders break into Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home in royal security breach
summary: A security breach at Prince William and Kate Middleton’s Sandringham Estate home raises fresh concerns over royal protection as police investigate.
story: Fox News' Greg Palkot reports on a security breach at the royal family's country home.
Police are investigating a security breach at Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home in England after intruders broke into the property on Monday night.

On Tuesday, Norfolk Constabulary confirmed that two men were arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespass in connection with the incident at Anmer Hall, which is located on King Charles’ Sandringham Estate.
"Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary following an incident at a property on the Sandringham Estate last night," police said in a statement to Fox News.
MEGHAN MARKLE COULD BE DRAGGED INTO FATHER’S CHILD SEX ABUSE CASE, EXPERT WARNS
The country home of Prince William, Prince of Wales and Catherine, Princess of Wales was subject to a security breach on Monday. (Karwai Tang/WireImage via Getty Images)

"Police were called just before 6 p.m. [local time] following a report of suspicious activity at the address," the statement continued. "Officers attended and specialist resources, including police dogs, drones and the National Police Air Service helicopter, were deployed to assist with searches in the area."
Authorities noted that the two suspects remain in police custody and confirmed that "the property was unoccupied at the time of the incident," adding that "inquiries remain ongoing."
William, Kate, and their three children — Prince George, Princess Charlotte, and Prince Louis — were staying at Forest Lodge in Windsor, The Sun reported.

Prince William and Princess Catherine were not home at the time of the break-in. (Getty Images)
The family relocated to the eight-bedroom Georgian mansion in Windsor Great Park in late 2025, calling it their "forever home" after moving from nearby Adelaide Cottage.
Ahead of that move, officials established a permanent public exclusion zone around a section of the park to bolster the family's security.
Fox News Digital has reached out to Kensington Palace for comment.
Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom residence on the 20,000-acre Sandringham Estate, was given to William and Kate as a wedding gift by the late Queen Elizabeth II.

Prior to moving in, the couple oversaw a £1.5 million renovation that included major security upgrades, such as rerouting a public road, planting dense tree lines for privacy, and establishing a seasonal no-fly zone over the property.
The family of five often visits the estate for holidays and special occasions.  (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

Though it is no longer their primary residence, the family regularly visits the country estate for weekend getaways and school holidays, and it served as a private sanctuary for Kate during her cancer treatment in 2024.
The break-in raises fresh concerns over royal security, as William and his immediate family receive 24-hour armed protection as working royals.

title: Meghan Markle could be dragged into father’s child sex abuse case, expert warns
summary: Meghan Markle could be pulled into a criminal investigation involving her estranged father, according to experts. Thomas Markle Sr. was arrested on Nov. 6 in Florida.
story: Fox News correspondent Danamarie McNicholl discusses Thomas Markle’s court appearance on ‘Special Report.’
A criminal investigation involving Meghan Markle’s estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr., threatens to pull the Duchess of Sussex into her family’s legal troubles, according to experts.
A legal expert told Fox News Digital that authorities could seek her cooperation if they believe she possesses information relevant to the allegations against her father.

"She may decide to cooperate with the investigation and may agree to be interviewed, almost certainly under certain negotiated conditions," Los Angeles entertainment and trial attorney Jordan Matthews said. "If she decides not to cooperate, then she could be compelled to provide information in connection with a subpoena."
Prince Harry could also be pulled into the investigation, but his communications with Meghan would likely be protected, according to Matthews.
MEGHAN MARKLE SAYS SHE KEPT FATHER AWAY FROM KIDS TO 'PROTECT' THEM OVER 'DISTURBING ALLEGATIONS' AGAINST HIM

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle were spotted for the first time after her father's arrest as the two arrived at the European Parliament for the opening of the Lost Screen Memorial on Nov. 10. (Omar Havana/Getty Images)

"Regardless, while he may also agree to cooperate, and while they will both likely take a public stance that they will cooperate and do anything necessary to protect the rights of children — even if Harry is not actually pulled into the investigation, he has already been pulled into the public fallout," Matthews, of Holtz Matthews LLP, explained. "Meghan and Harry are both obviously not immune from negative press coverage."
Fox News Digital reached out to Archewell for comment.
Federal prosecutors charged Markle Sr. with one count of possessing child sexual abuse material in a criminal complaint filed Nov. 5 before he was arrested in Florida.

According to the 14-page complaint obtained by Fox News Digital, FBI agents searched two storage units registered to Markle Sr. and seized approximately 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books containing suspected child sexual abuse material. Investigators say Markle Sr. had rented the units since 2008 and continued paying for them through October 2026.

Agents identified approximately 18 suspected illegal images among film negatives recovered from one unit. A witness, who had known Markle Sr. since the 1970s, allegedly identified him as the adult man appearing with a prepubescent girl in at least two photographs. The complaint did not name the witness.
Meghan Markle's mother, Doria Ragland, reportedly helped the FBI in the investigation against her ex-husband Thomas Markle. (Kevin Mazur)

However, reports have since surfaced that Meghan's mom played a key role in the arrest of her ex-husband. Doria Ragland helped federal agents identify Markle Sr. in photos seized in the ongoing child pornography investigation, according to People magazine. The outlet reported Meghan is prepared to assist the FBI in the investigation if needed.

Ragland and Markle Sr. were married in 1979 and later divorced in 1987. The couple reportedly met in the late 1970s while working in television in Los Angeles. Markle Sr. was a lighting director, while Ragland worked as a makeup artist. Meghan was born in 1981.
WATCH: MEGHAN MARKLE'S ESTRANGED FATHER RULED COMPETENT TO STAND TRIAL IN CHILD SEX ABUSE CASE
Investigators believe Markle Sr. could be in his 30s or 40s in the photographs, according to The Sun. The photos reportedly could have been taken when Meghan was young or before she was born.

The Philippine National Police in Cebu also filed criminal complaints on Nov. 17 accusing Markle Sr. of two counts of offering, distributing, selling, exporting or importing child sexual abuse or exploitation material, along with one count of possessing such material.

Markle Sr., who faces up to 20 years in prison if convicted in the U.S., had initially been released on bail before being detained again this month after allegedly cutting off his electronic monitoring tag. On Nov. 19, a federal court deemed him mentally competent to stand trial following a court-ordered psychiatric evaluation. He is scheduled to appear for a preliminary hearing in Florida on Dec. 1.
Thomas Markle Sr. was arrested Nov. 6. (GC Images)

The investigation began after Markle Sr.'s son, Thomas Markle Jr., reported finding storage boxes containing suspected child sexual abuse images at his father's local residence and turned the materials over to authorities.

Relatives have since claimed Markle Sr.’s trips to the region were an open family secret. Bobby Lucero, the son of Markle Sr.’s first wife, Roslyn Loveless, told The Sunday Times he grew up hearing stories from his mother and half-siblings about Markle Sr. visiting the Philippines on what they called his "girls trip." Lucero’s stepfather, Anthony Gonzales, also recalled hearing that Markle Sr. "liked young girls," though he told the outlet he never suspected at the time it involved minors.
Markle Sr. previously denied the allegations against him in a statement to the Daily Mail.

"I’m shocked, I’m hurt, and I’m very upset that my son is making these accusations against me," he was quoted as saying. "I could never do what I’m being accused of. It’s the worst thing anyone could accuse me of."

Meghan Markle is pictured with her husband, Prince Harry, and her mom, Doria Ragland. Ragland and Thomas Markle Sr. divorced in 1987. (Steve Parsons/Getty Images)
The allegations have added another painful chapter to Meghan's years-long estrangement from her father.

"While Thomas Markle Sr. is presumed innocent until proven guilty and Meghan Markle hasn’t been accused of any involvement in any alleged offenses, it is nevertheless definitely tarnishing to be from such a family," British royal expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital. "Men who behave in such a manner with women so much younger forever tarnish their family."

"Prosecutors could request statements, letters, or other records Meghan Markle has made, but one could anticipate differences depending on laws in the U.S., Philippines, or elsewhere," she added. "To date, there aren’t public reports of Meghan Markle being subpoenaed yet. She thus far is merely a family member who received prior allegations."
WATCH: MEGHAN MARKLE'S FATHER ARRESTED BY FBI OVER CHILD PORNOGRAPHY CHARGES
Meghan condemned the alleged abuse in October and explained her decision to cut ties with her father.

"I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed," she said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital at the time.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications' distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them," she wrote. "I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families."

"Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children."
Meghan Markle's estranged father was charged with one federal count of possessing child sexual abuse material. (2025 Getty Images)
Fox News Digital previously reported Buckingham Palace was blindsided by Markle Sr.'s arrest.

"I can tell you so far I’ve spoken to the palace, and they are not commenting on this and reinstating the fact that these two, Meghan and Harry, remain private citizens and, as such, this is a private matter for her family," royal commentator Neil Sean told Fox News Digital.

While the allegations have thrust Meghan's family back into the headlines, royal observers say the palace would be wise to keep its distance.

"The Royal Family cannot be expected to answer for the alleged criminal behavior of Meghan Markle’s father," royal expert Kinsey Schofield told Fox News Digital. "But there are legitimate questions about the handling of sensitive information when Harry and Meghan were working members of the institution. Those questions deserve answers, although they should never distract from the investigation itself."
WATCH: KING CHARLES MAY PRIVATELY SUPPORT MEGHAN MARKLE AMID CONTROVERSY: EXPERT
Despite the renewed scrutiny, Schofield emphasized that Meghan should not be held accountable for her father's alleged actions.

"Meghan Markle has spent years trying to distance herself from her father’s public controversies," Schofield explained. "But this is something far more serious than an embarrassing family dispute. Nobody should be held responsible for the alleged crimes of a relative. What matters now is whether any relevant information was properly reported and whether investigators have everything they need."

title: Billy Bob Thornton says he’s a holiday ‘purist’ as he brings back ‘traditional’ Thanksgiving at home
summary: Billy Bob Thornton says one restaurant Thanksgiving was enough, as his family returns to traditional cooking, football and holiday rituals at home.
story: "The Mayflower" host Billy Bob Thornton tells Fox News Digital why eating out on Thanksgiving just doesn’t hit the same.
Billy Bob Thornton tried to have Thanksgiving dinner at a restaurant in the past, and he'll never do it again.

During an interview with Fox News Digital about his new Fox Nation series, "The Mayflower," Thornton opened up about his own Thanksgiving traditions and how his newest gig shows the actual events that unfolded in 1621, not what is taught in schools.

"Well, I've always been a little bit of a purist in terms of holidays and, especially when you have kids, you want to kind of, you know, keep that tradition going. So my early thanksgivings were in Arkansas, and then after high school I moved to Texas and Houston," he began. "I've always wanted traditional holidays and particularly Thanksgiving and Christmas. And we have that, my family and I always have a traditional Christmas and Thanksgiving."
Billy Bob Thornton hosts "The Mayflower" on Fox Nation, which premieres on Nov. 23. (Fox Nation)
He continued, "But for Thanksgiving, a couple of times over the last decade, we went to a restaurant, and it just didn't seem right."
BILLY BOB THORNTON PUSHES BACK ON CELEBRITY ACTIVISM: ‘I DON'T KNOW ANYTHING ABOUT POLITICS’
Thornton said his wife and sister-in-law were tired of the mess that Thanksgiving creates in the kitchen, so they proposed the idea that they go out for dinner instead.

"We get there, and it was just like, we do this all the time, what's special about it, you know? And so this year, we're going back to the traditional thing and there's going to be a lot of cooking going on and a lot of football-watching," Thornton said.
Thornton hosts and narrates "The Mayflower," which is a three-part historical docudrama. It premieres Monday, Nov. 23, on FOX Nation.
Thornton said that part of the series was shot on a replica of the Mayflower. (Matei Horvath/Getty Images)
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Speaking to Fox News Digital, the Academy Award-winning actor explained that once he was brought on to this project, he learned about the reality of the journey on the Mayflower and the extent of the "pain, suffering and sickness" people endured.
WATCH: BILLY BOB THORNTON SAYS HE REFUSES TO DO THANKSGIVING AT A RESTAURANT

"I would say the fact that not everybody who came over here, they weren't all exactly buddies. You know, there were people who just hitched a ride and all this kind of stuff. And also just learning to what extent there actually was pain and suffering and sickness. By the end of the first winter, half of those people were gone. I mean, that was surprising," he said.
Thornton explained that the Fox Nation series created a replica of the ship, which was much smaller than he expected.
Thornton told Fox News Digital he learned a lot about the first Thanksgiving when creating this series. (Scott Dudelson/Getty Images for Stagecoach)

"We did stuff on the replica of the Mayflower. It's not a big ship, I mean, at all, and to go down below deck there and see where these people were, and they were literally on top of each other – I mean, it was crowded getting the crew down there to film anything. And so it really brings it home to you about how difficult this really was," he said.
Thornton said he wasn't aware of the "bloodshed" that surrounded the Mayflower's journey to America.
WATCH: BILLY BOB THORNTON ON THE DARK HISTORY BEHIND THE FIRST THANKSGIVING

"I mean, I've heard things, but you know, like it says in the documentary, most of us, in terms of Thanksgiving, know what we learned in the third and fourth grade," he continued. "And it was all just like, 'Oh, look, look at the Native people. Let's invite them over for dinner, you know, and make peace.' And it wasn't like that. I mean, there was a war involved in this."
Thornton told Fox News Digital one of the main reasons he signed on to this series was because it was intended to educate people.
Billy Bob Thornton is an Academy Award-winning actor. (Jim Smeal/Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

"To be a part of something like this, to actually host something that educates you – and believe me, it educated me. I learned as I went along – I did not know this story. And so I just love being a part and telling a story that people don't know about," he said.
WATCH: BILLY BOB THORNTON EXPLORES AMERICA'S ORIGIN IN FOX NATION'S ‘THE MAYFLOWER’ SERIES
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
The actor is really hoping this docudrama hits home with young people, so they can remember the true meaning of Thanksgiving.
Billy Bob Thornton said he loves being a part of something that tells a story "that people don't know about." (Fox Nation)

"I think the more young people that watch this, the better. I think it would be really good for young people to see this and to understand where we come from and exactly how difficult it was and to maybe appreciate their forefathers and even within their own families," he told Fox News Digital.

title: 'Platoon' star Tom Berenger disses Hollywood as a 'company town,' praises Florida life
summary: Tom Berenger explains why he never lived in Hollywood, calling it a tedious "company town," and shared why he vastly prefers Florida and South Carolina.
story: The "Platoon" actor spoke to Fox News Digital about his new docuseries "Ronin 3: The Battle for Sangin."
Tom Berenger said he never liked the idea of living in Hollywood because he always felt that it was like a "company" town where everyone had the same job and talked shop constantly.

"I never lived in Hollywood," the "Platoon" actor told Fox News Digital recently. "I started in New York in the theater, and I always lived there. And I knew all those New York actors, you know, John Heard, Chris Walken. And a few guys are gone: Brian Dennehy, Peter Weller. And we all hung out together at times, but none of us really liked Hollywood."

They all saw Los Angeles as a "company town where all people did was talk about it all the time," he explained. "I guess it'd be like being in Detroit if they all talked about cars constantly. I don't know. But it was boring to us. It was tedious… it wasn't about anything."
CHRIS ROCK EXPOSES LA'S DARK ‘UNDERBELLY’ THAT PEOPLE PRETEND DOESN'T EXIST
Tom Berenger says he always saw Los Angeles as a "company town." (Getty Images for TCM)
He said New York is a "whole different place" that has an identity outside of theater.
These days, Berenger calls Florida home, which he said he vastly prefers to L.A.

"And South Carolina, it was better too," he said of where he lived for three decades. "They have other jobs and real jobs, for one thing, and it's not the same old chit-chat, I guess. They look different. The people are nicer… I could go on probably for hours if I had to."
Berenger recently narrated "Ronin 3: The Battle for Sangin," a docuseries about a platoon’s experience in Afghanistan.
The series was released on Veterans Day and is available on Prime Video.

Tom Berenger with Oliver Stone, Willem Dafoe and Charlie Sheen in 2006 celebrating the 20th anniversary of the release of "Platoon" at the Cannes Film Festival. (WireImage)
While they were shooting the movie in the Philippines, Berenger said he had to go to Sheen’s hotel room to ask him something, and he saw he had a stereo system with speakers and a CD player.

"I go, ‘What is all this stuff, Charlie?'" he said, adding that it was the type of equipment someone would have in their house, not while traveling.

Sheen told him that his mother sent it all to him, and he had kept the boxes and would mail it all back before he left.

title: Russell Brand's wife vows to 'honor' prison rules after comedian's 'not guilty' message sparks investigation
summary: Laura Brand says she will honor HMP Littlehey's rules after reading Russell Brand's "not guilty" message, which officials say is urgently investigated.
story: Fox News senior foreign affairs correspondent Greg Palkot reports on Russell Brand's 10-year sentencing after his conviction for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others. The judge criticized Brand's conduct, while his attorneys are expected to appeal the verdict.

One week after Russell Brand's wife, Laura, sparked a government investigation by broadcasting a "not guilty" message from her imprisoned husband, she is pledging to follow prison communication rules while standing by her family.

Laura addressed the incident during the Nov. 22 episode of the couple's weekly Sunday Service YouTube vlog, telling viewers she will "honor" the rules set in place for her husband — who was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault.

"Last week’s episode drew a considerable amount of attention," Laura said. "And now that I understand the parameters set by the brilliant and professional staff at HMP Littlehey, I will absolutely honor that."
RUSSELL BRAND’S WIFE OPENS UP AFTER COMEDIAN’S RAPE CONVICTION, SHARES MESSAGE FROM IMPRISONED HUSBAND
Russell Brand's wife, Laura, addressed the online backlash after reading her husband's claim of innocence from behind prison bars. (Russell Brand YouTube; Getty Images)

"I will continue to be proud to be a wife, a mother and a woman defending her family at a time when the media’s image of what kind of a woman I am is under so much scrutiny," she said.
Last week, Brand claimed he was "not guilty" in a message read by Laura during an episode of "Sunday Service."
Russell Brand arrives at Southwark Crown Court in London on Oct. 29, 2026, ahead of his trial on rape and sexual assault charges. He has denied all charges. (Getty Images)
RUSSELL BRAND SPARKS PRISON INVESTIGATION AFTER WIFE READS DEFIANT MESSAGE FOLLOWING RAPE CONVICTION

Shortly after the message was shared publicly, a spokesperson for British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in a statement to Deadline, "This is clearly appalling and is being urgently investigated. We expect action to be taken if he’s found to have broken the rules."

"Prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims, and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances. Prisoners cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments."

On Nov. 16, Lord Chancellor and Secretary of State Alex Norris wrote on X, "The broadcast of a statement from Russell Brand is completely unacceptable. Prisoners are rightly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims."

RUSSELL BRAND POLICE INTERROGATION VIDEO EMERGES AS NEW RAPE INVESTIGATIONS LOOM AFTER CONVICTION

According to regulations governing prisons in England and Wales, authorities can restrict a prisoner's contact with the outside world. In the message, Brand maintained his innocence while confirming he is currently being jailed at HMP Littlehey, a prison for individuals who have been convicted of sexual offenses.

The good news is that I have already seen that the staff here are strong, they are kind, and they are dedicated," she continued. "And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone."

"I don’t know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that Christ died to save, like you and me. Let us all love, pray for, and forgive one another as God forgave us."
"Please support my treasured wife and family. I feel your prayers, your brother in Christ. Russell," she concluded.

title: John Malkovich recalls losing 'pretty much everything' to Bernie Madoff's Ponzi scheme
summary: John Malkovich opens up to "60 Minutes" about losing his entire fortune to Bernie Madoff's Ponzi scheme and the moment he told his wife the news.
story: FOX Business' Charlie Gasparino joins 'Your World' to discuss the downfall of the former American financier
John Malkovich recalled once losing his entire fortune to disgraced financier Bernie Madoff.
Malkovich, 72, told "60 Minutes" that he had recently returned from directing a play in Mexico City when he found out about Madoff's Ponzi scheme.

"I got home from that and I saw this photograph of Bernie Madoff in handcuffs, and I thought, 'Oh, well that could prove interesting,'" Malkovich said. "I went in and said to my wife, you know, 'I'm just going to go around the corner, buy a pack of cigarettes.'"
FRAUD MASTERMIND BEHIND MULTIMILLION-DOLLAR PONZI SCHEME THAT VICTIMIZED TRAVIS KELCE IS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT
John Malkovich was one of many victims of late disgraced financier Bernie Madoff's Ponzi scheme. (Swan Gallet)
He added, "I said, 'We have a little problem. Bernie Madoff just got arrested.'"
Malkovich, a previous smoker, hadn't indulged in nicotine "for a while" when he left the house that day, he said.

"That was pretty much everything I'd ever made," he admitted before coming to terms with his situation. "You know, you look to blame, you're going to do this and that, and then you realize, 'Look, why don't you shut up?'"
FORMER DISNEY STAR ERIK VON DETTEN SUED FOR ELDER ABUSE AFTER COUPLE POURED $2.1M RETIREMENT SAVINGS INTO GOLD
"Whatever you lost, most people who were ever born will never have a 10th of that, no matter what they do. No matter what they do. Get on with your life and that's it."
Madoff died in April 2021 while serving a 150-year sentence at the federal medical care center in Butner, North Carolina, where his attorney said he was being treated for terminal kidney failure.

A decades-long force on Wall Street, Madoff shocked the world when he pleaded guilty in 2009 to running a vast Ponzi scheme that prosecutors said swindled thousands out of their life savings. The scheme began in the early 1970s, and by the time Madoff was arrested in December 2008, had defrauded as many as 37,000 people in 136 countries out of up to $65 billion.
His victims included the famous – director Steven Spielberg, actor Kevin Bacon and Nobel Peace Prize winner Elie Wiesel – as well as ordinary investors.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Madoff said he started the fraud, in which he appeared to deliver steady returns to clients, but was actually using money from new investors to pay off existing shareholders, in the 1990s because he felt "compelled" to give investors solid returns despite the recession and weak stock market. Prosecutors contend he started defrauding investors much earlier.
Bernard "Bernie" Madoff pleaded guilty in 2009 to running a massive Ponzi scheme. (Mario Tama/Getty Images)
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"When I began the Ponzi scheme, I believed it would end shortly and I would be able to extricate myself and my clients," Madoff told the judge at his plea hearing. "However, this proved difficult, and ultimately impossible, and as the years went by, I realized that my arrest and this day would inevitably come."

Prior to his downfall, Madoff was viewed as a self-made and respected figure among financial professionals as the head of the seemingly successful Bernard L. Madoff Investment Securities firm. He also served as the chairman of the Nasdaq Stock Market in 1990, 1991 and 1993.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

In addition to being sentenced to the maximum 150 years in prison, Madoff and his family took a major financial hit: A judge issued a $171 billion forfeiture order in June 2009 requiring the disgraced financier to give up his interests in all property, including real estate, investments, cars and boats. Under the arrangement, the government also obtained his wife's interest in all property, including $80 million that she claimed belonged to her, leaving Ruth Madoff with $2.5 million in assets.
Madoff died in April 2021 while serving a 150-year sentence at the federal medical care center in Butner, North Carolina. (Bureau of Prisons)

The decline and fall of Madoff also took a toll on his family. The oldest of his two sons, Mark Madoff, died by suicide on the second anniversary of his father's arrest in 2010. His other son, Andrew, died from cancer at age 48 in 2014.
Mark Madoff's suicide prompted his mother, Ruth Madoff, to cut off all communications with her husband.

"I was responsible for my son Mark's death and that's very, very difficult," Madoff said during a 2013 interview with CNN. "I live with that. I live with the remorse, the pain I caused everybody, certainly my family, and the victims."

title: 'Yes, Dear' star Anthony Clark's cause of death revealed: report
summary: Anthony Clark's cause of death was septic shock, with influenza A and chronic alcoholism as underlying conditions and acute kidney failure a factor.
story: "Yes Dear" star Anthony Clark died on Tuesday, Nov. 10. He was 62. (Getty Images)
Anthony Clark's official cause of death was due to septic shock, according to a death certificate obtained by People magazine. He was 62.
The "Yes, Dear" star died on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Influenza A and chronic alcoholism were included as underlying conditions, the outlet reported.
In addition, acute kidney failure was listed as a significant contributing factor in Clark's death.
'YES, DEAR' STAR ANTHONY CLARK DEAD AT 62
Anthony Clark's cause of death was revealed to be due to septic shock. (Getty Images)
"Anthony was one of the funniest and most talented comedians and actors I have ever had the pleasure of watching," his longtime manager, Barry Katz, told Fox News Digital.

"It was an honor to represent him and he will be missed for the joy, happiness, and love he brought to everyone he worked with and the audiences that were blessed to see his undeniable performances."

Clark's "Yes, Dear" co-star, Mike O'Malley, initially shared the news of his death in a tribute posted on X. Deadline then reported that Clark died of "complications related to pneumonia and the flu."
Anthony Clark starred alongside Jean Louisa Kelly and Mike O'Malley in "Yes, Dear." (CBS via Getty Images)

STACY KEACH DEAD AT 85 AS ‘MIKE HAMMER’ STAR’S WIFE SHARES EMOTIONAL TRIBUTE

He had us laughing loudly once again. Attached are some snapshots from our last episode of Yes Dear, which ended 20 years ago after 122 episodes. Rest in peace. Tony."

His film credits include "Dogfight," "The Thing Called Love" and "The Rock." He also appeared on "Ellen" and hosted the fourth season of "Last Comic Standing" in 2006.

title: 'I Dream of Jeannie' star Barbara Eden, 95, still rides exercise bike for 35 minutes to stay fit
summary: Barbara Eden reveals the stationary bike routine and personal trainer workouts keeping her fit as the "I Dream of Jeannie" star turns 95.
story: Barbara Eden, who starred on "I Dream of Jeannie" in the 1960s, still works out with a personal trainer at 95 years old.  (Silver Screen Collection/Getty Images; Franziska Krug/Getty Images for Marcel Remus)
Barbara Eden isn’t slowing down at all — she's actually speeding up.
Despite turning 95 in August, the "I Dream of Jeannie" icon stays fit by working out on her stationary bicycle.
"I go for about, I don't know, 35 minutes on the bike," Eden told Fox News Digital recently of her fitness routine. "It's good."
BARBARA EDEN, 95, SAYS SHE’S ‘OKAY’ AFTER LAST-MINUTE CANCELATION OF FESTIVAL APPEARANCE
Barbara Eden does a workout on a beach in 1964. (Getty Images)
The former sitcom star said that both she and her husband of 35 years, Jon Eicholtz, both have a personal trainer who comes to their home.
"I don't go to the gym anymore," she revealed, adding that when she did, it was "spinning class for an hour, and then I worked with a trainer for a half hour, lifting weights."
DONNA MILLS DOES 100 SIT-UPS A DAY, PLAYS TENNIS FIVE TIMES A WEEK AT 85 BUT WON'T QUIT DORITOS
Eden said she still lifts weights a little. "Not as heavy as I used to." She added that weightlifting is especially good for women and their bones.
"You have to be disciplined about being active when you’re an actor," she laughed when asked. "My husband and I both have a trainer that comes in and helps us out."
4 SIMPLE HABITS CAN HELP SLOW MUSCLE LOSS AS YOU AGE, FITNESS EXPERT SAYS
Eden said she wasn’t sure what to credit for her longevity and energy, "but I'm glad I'm here, and I'm glad I'm still working."
Eden starred as Jeannie on the sitcom, which ran from 1965 until 1970. (Getty)

"I'm careful about what I eat, but I'm not overly stupid about it, you know?" she said when asked about her diet and philosophy on health. "I've never smoked. I don't know if that means anything. But, I think one of the things that's most important in your life is that you recognize other people. You realize that they're not so different than you are and that you have to get along. And when you do that, you find life is much more interesting, and people are much more interesting."
The actress also has a simple beauty routine which she said is what she’s always done. It involves washing her face at night and putting on moisturizer.
"That's about it," she revealed.

One thing the timeless beauty said she wished she had known about when she was younger was "the damage the sun could do to your skin. We didn't know that when I was growing up. And I think it really helps, if you know, to put sunscreen, you know, on your face during the day. Or if you're working."
The actress’ career spans more than 70 years, but she is best known for her titular role in the iconic sitcom "I Dream of Jeannie," which she said she never expected to become a phenomenon.
‘I DREAM OF JEANNIE’ STAR BARBARA EDEN TURNS HEADS AT 94 IN NEW PHOTO WITH HUSBAND
Barbara Eden poses for a photo as Jeannie on "I Dream of Jeannie." (Getty Images)
"It makes me so happy, really so happy that people still enjoy her," Eden said. "I really never expected the show to have the longevity it has."
The "Voyage to the Bottom of the Sea" star said that she gets fan mail from all over the world, including China and Russia.
‘CHARLIE’S ANGELS’ STAR JACLYN SMITH LIVED APART FROM HER HUSBAND FOR 17 YEARS DURING THEIR 35-YEAR LOVE STORY
"I'm just flabbergasted when I get the mail, and very, very proud. I just didn't expect it this long to be around."
Some fans even tell her that the show helped them through a difficult childhood.
WILLIAM SHATNER SAYS HE'S 'TAKING CARE OF BUSINESS' AT 95: 'THE LEAST OF ALL I WANT DO IS DIE'

"People will come up to me and say, ‘Oh, my God, you saved me when I was a child, because I had such a terrible childhood,’ and they just pour out what happened to them during their growing up period," she explained. "And so many of them were hurt either physically or mentally, and the show helped them. And I'm so happy to hear that."
Barbara Eden poses as Jeannie at an event in June. (Getty Images for Project Angel Food's Lead with Love 7)
One fan even revealed that they had turned their bedroom into a bottle as a refuge from the difficulties of life in the opulent style of Jeannie’s — where she slept on the show.
Eden also fondly remembers her "wonderful" co-star Larry Hagman, who played her love interest and "master" astronaut Anthony Nelson on the show.
"You never knew what was going to happen with Larry," she laughed, explaining that he was a bit of a prankster.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
"He was just fun and unexpectedly fun, you know, for a lot of people." she added. "He was a dear guy. Yes, he was. He was like working with a 12-year-old boy. That's what it was, yes."

Eden said she rarely hears criticism of the series, but one thing that does bother her is when people wonder: "‘Why did you call him your master? You know, you're not supposed to call him a master.’ You know, and that's so foolish. Look, it's a fantasy, you know, and it's magic. And we're not talking about the women working in the office or doing real things. And she's a genie!"
She treasures her five seasons on the show, but the one creative difference she had was Jeannie and Tony getting married in the last season.
Larry Hagman and Barbara Eden pose during the wedding episode of "I Dream of Jeannie" in 1969. (NBCUniversal via Getty Images)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"That is the one thing about the show that I was upset about," she admitted. "They should never have gotten married. I mean, you know, she thought she was human. And he knew she wasn't. They couldn't get married. They were too different. She was an entity, you know? He was a human. Yeah. So, no, they should never have been married."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
In her own life, however, she’s been happily married since 1991.

"Jon and I just, we respect each other’s lives, what we’re doing," she said of how they’ve stayed married so long. "We share together in our life. It's not like two different people. I can't tell you what it is, but if you love someone, you get the 35 years."
