title: Body washed ashore in Oregon identified as former city councilor missing since September plane crash
summary: Human remains that washed ashore on the Oregon coast were identified as Ralph H. Busby III, whose plane crashed into the Pacific Ocean in September.
story: Ralph H. Busby III, 78, served on the Newport City Council from 2013 to 2017. His body washed ashore on the coast near Newport on Nov. 15 after he vanished in a September plane crash into the Pacific Ocean. (Facebook/City of Newport)
Human remains that washed ashore along the Oregon coast last week have been identified as a 78-year-old former city councilor whose small plane crashed into the Pacific Ocean in September.

The Oregon State Medical Examiner's Office confirmed on Monday that the remains were identified as Ralph H. Busby III, FOX12 Oregon reported. Busby served on the Newport City Council from 2013 to 2017, the city said in a statement posted to its Facebook page on Monday.

Busby was the lone occupant of a twin-engine Beechcraft B95 that crashed about a mile west of Nye Beach near Newport shortly before 12:45 p.m. on Sept. 21, according to the U.S. Coast Guard Northwest District.
4 FLORIDA FAMILY MEMBERS FOUND DEAD AFTER SMALL PLANE GOES DOWN OFF THE BAHAMAS
Yaquina Bay bridge is seen near the harbor entrance of Newport, Oregon, on the central Oregon coast. (Don and Melinda Crawford/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images, File)

Eyewitness Yoshio Abe, who was fishing just south of the Yaquina Head Lighthouse, told the outlet in September that he noticed the plane flying unusually low, about 20 feet above the water, in a strange flight pattern before it hit the ocean.
"Within three minutes the head went down, and in 10 seconds the whole thing went down," Abe said.
The Coast Guard deployed a helicopter and search-and-rescue boats and covered around 124 square miles before suspending the search later that night.
A fishing wharf and dock with a welcome sign on the bay in Old Town Newport, Oregon. (Don and Melinda Crawford/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images, File)

The body was discovered in the surf near Yaquina Head Lighthouse on Nov. 15, Oregon State Police said. Weather and hazardous surf conditions kept state police and U.S. Coast Guard crews from recovering the remains for three days until the body washed ashore.
FLORIDA LEARJET CRASH INVESTIGATORS DIG UP ENGINE PIECE AFTER PILOTS WARNED OF ROUGH WEATHER AHEAD
Oregon State Police told the outlet that the National Transportation Safety Board has been notified as investigators continue looking into the Sept. 21 crash.

After officials identified the remains, the City of Newport posted its statement extending condolences to Busby's wife, Sharon, his family and friends. City officials noted his work on the Budget, Airport and Vision 2040 advisory committees and his advocacy for the Newport Municipal Airport.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"His dedication to the community and his willingness to give his time and experience helped guide Newport's future," the city said in its statement.
"We are grateful for Ralph's years of service to Newport and the lasting impacts he made on our community," it continued.

title: Marathoner asked husband about ‘powdery’ water before fatal fall – then police found his Google searches
summary: Benjamin Angus Carpenter faces first-degree intentional homicide in wife Erica Carpenter's death as prosecutors cite texts about "powdery" water.
story: Benjamin Angus Carpenter is charged with first-degree intentional homicide more than two years after his 40-year-old wife died following an alleged basement fall in West Allis, Wisconsin.

A Wisconsin man has been charged with killing his marathon-running wife more than two years after she died in an alleged basement fall – with prosecutors pointing to texts about "powdery" water, an ominous Google search and a new girlfriend.
The West Allis Police Department said Benjamin Angus Carpenter, 45, has been arrested and charged with first-degree intentional homicide in the October 2024 death of his wife, Erica A. Carpenter, 40.

Officers were dispatched to the couple's residence in the 2900 block of South 95th Street around 10:38 p.m. on Oct. 13, 2024, for a welfare check after a report that Erica had fallen and was bleeding from the head, according to a criminal complaint.
TEACHER FOUND DEAD WITH THROAT SLIT; DETECTIVES SCRUTINIZE HUSBAND’S SHIFTING STORY

When officers arrived, they found Carpenter performing CPR on his wife at the bottom of the basement stairs. Officers took over lifesaving efforts until rescue personnel arrived and transported her to Froedtert Hospital, where she was pronounced dead at 5:14 the next morning.
Benjamin Angus Carpenter, 45, is being held on a $500,000 cash bond after being charged with first-degree intentional homicide. (West Allis Police Department)

Carpenter told investigators Erica had felt dizzy and was having trouble breathing all day before collapsing while they were doing laundry in the basement, claiming they tumbled backwards down the stairs while he tried carrying her up and that she struck her head against a cinder block wall.
MISSOURI ASSISTANT FIRE CHIEF CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER HIDDEN VIDEO FOUND ON WIFE'S PHONE, INVESTIGATORS SAY

Police launched a death investigation that spanned more than two years, reviewing autopsy findings alongside searches of email accounts and cellphones before concluding Carpenter planned and caused her death.

While Erica's final cause of death was ruled undetermined, Milwaukee County Deputy Chief Medical Examiner Douglas Kelley told detectives her injuries – including neck cartilage fractures and hemorrhage – were suspicious for asphyxia and indicated blunt force trauma to the neck, the complaint states.
IVY LEAGUE-EDUCATED PEDIATRICIAN ALLEGEDLY MURDERED BY HUSBAND WHO THEN SET HOME ON FIRE: POLICE
Investigators also questioned Carpenter about his background as a Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt and whether choke submissions leave marks, to which he replied, "not that I've ever heard of."

Toxicology testing detected doxylamine, an over-the-counter sleep aid, and hydrocodone, a prescription opioid painkiller, in Erica's system. Less than two weeks before her death, Carpenter had texted Erica asking her to research melatonin or other sleep remedies for them – messages that were later deleted from his phone, investigators found.

Erica A. Carpenter, 40, was a healthcare worker and marathon runner who died in October 2024 after an alleged fall down the basement stairs of her West Allis home. (Credit: Facebook / Erica Carpenter)
‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT’S 100K TEXTS WITH MISTRESS SHOW MOTIVE IN WIFE’S MURDER, PROSECUTORS SAY
On the day Erica died, Carpenter searched Google for "can I crush pills and take them in water," prosecutors alleged.

Weeks earlier, on Sept. 18, 2024, Erica had confronted Carpenter over text about something in her drink, writing, "And what the f--- have you been doing to my water the past few days?!?!?" before adding, "There's been powdery s--- in it at least twice now."

On that same evening, records from Carpenter's Gmail account showed Google searches for "losing someone," and "watching someone you love die," investigators alleged.
Investigators also uncovered an affair with a coworker – a relationship Carpenter claimed he planned to tell Erica about before she died.
MISSOURI NURSE FOUND DEAD MONTHS AFTER ANESTHESIOLOGIST HUSBAND ADMITTED TO ASSAULTING WOMAN

Erica A. Carpenter, 40, died Oct. 14, 2024. Prosecutors say deleted text messages show she had questioned her husband about putting powder in her drinks weeks before her death. (Facebook / Erica Carpenter)

Instead, his actions immediately after Erica's death painted a far different picture. The couple's son told investigators he was introduced to his father's new girlfriend the very next day when she brought dinner over. Within roughly four weeks, Carpenter had taken down photos of Erica in the kitchen, and by December 2024 or January 2025, the woman had moved into the home.

That relationship later drew police back to the same house in May 2025 when the girlfriend alleged Carpenter placed his hand around her neck and strangled her, and again in October 2025 after she flagged down an Uber driver with facial injuries and said Carpenter had struck her roughly 10 times.

Financial records pointed to a similar contradiction in the weeks right after Erica's funeral. Between Oct. 28 and Nov. 13, 2024, Carpenter spent more than $4,000 at Jared Jewelers, including $3,754 on a diamond bracelet just three days after laying his wife to rest – where an assistant manager told police he was shopping for an engagement ring for his new girlfriend and claimed his wife died from a flu shot complication.

Yet two days after buying the bracelet, he called State Farm Insurance claiming funeral expenses had left him unable to pay his mortgage or car note, prosecutors said. At the same time, he collected more than $220,000 from his wife's employer-provided life insurance policy – despite telling police he did not know she had one – while pressing State Farm about a separate $300,000 policy and collecting money from a benefit pub crawl and a GoFundMe campaign.

Away from the case file, Erica worked in healthcare and drew national attention in April 2020 when she mapped out and ran her own solo marathon after her scheduled race was canceled during the COVID-19 pandemic, NBC News reported at the time. She later ran the 2023 Chicago Marathon to raise money for the Organization for Autism Research.

Carpenter made his initial court appearance Nov. 18, where a court commissioner set his cash bond at $500,000 and placed him under JusticePoint Level 5 supervision with no firearms or dangerous weapons if released, court records show.

He has not yet entered a plea and is due back in court for a preliminary hearing on Dec. 8, records show.

title: Lindsay Clancy prosecutors ask court to delay her retrial in children's stranglings
summary: Plymouth County prosecutors are asking the state's highest court to pause Lindsay Clancy's March retrial while her double jeopardy appeal plays out.
story: Television host Nancy Grace discusses Lindsay Clancy's upcoming March trial, the allegations surrounding the deaths of her three young children and the legal questions at the center of the case.

With the clock ticking toward Lindsay Clancy's March retrial in the strangling deaths of her three children — and the judge's mandatory retirement in June — it's Plymouth County prosecutors who are asking Massachusetts' highest court to pause the proceedings while her defense raises a double jeopardy appeal.

"The full Court will presumably determine whether such a retrial will violate the defendant’s double jeopardy rights," wrote Assistant Plymouth County District Attorney Melissa Johnsen. "As such, it makes little sense to move forward with proceedings intended to bring the defendant to a trial, where this Court may ultimately decide that a retrial is barred by double jeopardy."
Johnsen added that it would be "ambitious" to believe the appeal would be resolved in time for jury selection in her retrial, currently scheduled for March 29.
LINDSAY CLANCY TO BE RETRIED FOR MURDER IN KILLING OF THREE CHILDREN
Defendant Lindsay Clancy listens during her murder trial at Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth, Mass., on Thursday, July 30, 2026. (CJ Gunther/The Boston Herald via AP, Pool)
Clancy's lawyers, Kevin Reddington and Martin Weinberg, have opposed the idea, writing to the state's Supreme Judicial Court that "she wants to keep her trial date."

While prosecutors had argued that a stay in the trial court would "forego any additional expense and effort" in preparations, Clancy's lawyers countered that "the cost of a stay would fall on Ms. Clancy, who is held without bail."
LINDSAY CLANCY'S LAWYER REVEALS POST-MISTRIAL STRATEGY AS RETRIAL LOOMS

Her appeal centers on the argument that it wasn't necessary for Judge William Sullivan to declare a mistrial with jurors deadlocked 11-1 on Sept. 4, and as a result she is facing unconstitutional double jeopardy with the case slated for a second trial.
PROSECUTORS REVEAL SIX LINDSAY CLANCY JURY NOTES AS THEY FIGHT BID TO DISMISS MURDER CHARGES
The lone holdout, whom other panelists accused of ignoring reasonable doubt and insisting Clancy was guilty anyway, could have been replaced with an alternate, according to Reddington.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
Callan, left, Dawson and Cora Clancy. The three children were killed at their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

Michael Desronvil, the only juror who voted to find her guilty, has denied such allegations and said in a recent Fox News interview that he believed Clancy had meticulously planned to murder her children — Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months — while her then-husband was running errands.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

Sullivan wrote that he was skeptical of the other jurors' allegations, denied the defense request to replace Desronvil and declared a mistrial after a week of stalled deliberations. Then he denied defense motions to hold an inquiry into Desronvil, finding that it would be inappropriate to interfere with jury deliberations, and another motion to dismiss the case on double jeopardy grounds.
LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL HOLDOUT SAYS HE THOUGHT SHE WAS 'METHODICAL' IN THE 'EXECUTION' OF HER CHILDREN

Patrick Clancy exits Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., Monday, July 27, 2026. His ex-wife, Lindsay Clancy, was on trial for the murder of their three children, but it ended in a mistrial after jurors deadlocked for a week. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
SEND US A TIP

The defense appealed to Justice Elizabeth Dewar, who last week referred the case to the full Supreme Judicial Court. Plymouth County prosecutors asked the court Monday to stay the retrial as her appeal plays out.
GOT A TIP?

"The prosecution's position is probably based on the difficulty of deciding a full bench appeal and getting ready for trial No. 2 so quickly," said Jack Lu, a retired Massachusetts judge and legal scholar who has been following the case. "I see this as a reasonable request, and the parties have not even publicly stated, after setting the actual trial date, that they will really be ready."
LINDSAY CLANCY HIRES KAREN READ ATTORNEY FOR HIGH-STAKES DOUBLE JEOPARDY FIGHT AFTER MURDER MISTRIAL

Lindsay Clancy and her attorney, Kevin Reddington, attend a status hearing for the Clancy case at the Plymouth County Superior Court in Plymouth, Massachusetts on Sept. 29, 2026. (Greg Derr / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Prosecutors will likely have to recruit a new team of experts and revise their approach after the first trial ended with 11 of the 12 jurors siding with the defense.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

Superior Court Judge William Sullivan presides over day three of jury selection Wednesday, July 22, 2026, in the triple murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, who was accused of murdering her three young children in 2023 in their Duxbury, Massachusetts home. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via Pool)
LINDSAY CLANCY PROSECUTORS FACE DILEMMA: RETRIAL OR PLEA DEAL IN CASE INVOLVING 3 STRANGLED CHILDREN

Under Massachusetts law, Sullivan will reach the age of mandatory retirement in June, prompting some experts to question whether prosecutors are aiming to delay the retrial long enough to try it under a new judge.

"The biggest question is are your experts locked in," Lu said. "So, I do not think they are judge shopping which, contrary to what some believe, is a part of litigation."

title: California dad falls 500 feet to his death after saving son on icy mountain trail
summary: Guillermo Batres, 44, fell about 500 feet on Mount Baden-Powell after rescuing his son, leaving family grieving as a GoFundMe nears $25,000.
story: Two Colorado Mountain College students plunged to their deaths while rappelling down West Apostle Mountain. Investigators now believe a rock securing their equipment gave way, sending both climbers falling.
While hiking Mount Baden-Powell in the San Gabriel Mountains, a California father fell roughly 500 feet to his death after helping his son recover from a slip on the ice.
Guillermo Alejandro Batres, 44, lost his life while attempting to summit the 9,407-foot peak on Sunday, according to a GoFundMe set up by his niece, Jennifer.
After October, conditions on Mount Baden-Powell can shift rapidly from a standard, intermediate hike to hazardous winter terrain, as snow and ice quickly accumulate along its shaded, steep slopes.
Batres' son slipped on the ice and as Batres went to pull him up, that's when he fell himself, the family said.
Guillermo Alejandro Batres, 44, died on Sunday, Nov. 22, after falling during a hike with his son at Mount Baden-Powell. (GoFundMe)
MOUNTAIN CLIMBER SURVIVES TERRIFYING 500-FOOT FALL IN CALIFORNIA'S SIERRA NEVADA, NIGHT STRANDED ON LEDGE

"As Guillermo tried to help him up, he slipped on ice and fell approximately 500 feet down a steep gulch. Guillermo died in the fall, leaving his family shocked, grieving, and facing an unimaginable loss," Jennifer wrote in the GoFundMe description.
As of Tuesday morning, the online fundraiser had pulled in more than $25,000 toward its $40,000 goal.
The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner ruled Batres' death an accident and said he died from blunt force injuries.
Batres was an avid hiker and runner, having become a certified ultrarunning coach in July 2025. (GoFundMe)
FAMILY'S SPRING BREAK HIKE TURNS INTO LIFE-OR-DEATH RESCUE AFTER PARENT FALLS 70 FEET OFF UTAH CLIFF
Batres had a following on Instagram, where he frequently posted about his passion for running and hiking.

In July 2025, Batres became a certified ultrarunning coach — a specialist who helps runners build the endurance needed for races longer than a traditional 26.2-mile marathon, which can stretch for multiple days and stretch for up to 100 miles.
Batres fell to his death after saving his son from the same fate after the boy slipped on ice. (GoFundMe)

An avid hiker and outdoorsman, Batres also founded Clean Plug Sneaker Cleaner, his own brand of shoe-cleaning products.

title: Putin's war death toll reportedly tops 700,000 as Russia scrambles for recruits
summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov dismisses an investigation estimating 700,000 Russian troops have died in Vladimir Putin's war against Ukraine.
story: Footage supplied by East2West shows reportedly destroyed Russian military aircraft in August 2026.

The Kremlin on Wednesday dismissed a new investigation estimating that at least 700,000 Russian troops have died in President Vladimir Putin's war against Ukraine, as experts warn that mounting military losses are undermining Moscow's ability to sustain its offensive.
The findings, published Monday by independent Russian news outlets Meduza and Mediazona, are based on leaked Russian government records and statistical analysis.
"The only entity that can officially disclose casualty figures is the Russian Defense Ministry," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters Wednesday, according to The Moscow Times.
PUTIN'S WAR MACHINE TIED TO TROUBLING RECRUITMENT OF YOUNG WOMEN AS NEW DEALS EMERGE
Russian soldiers ride a truck during a rehearsal for the Victory Day military parade at the Dvortsovaya (Palace) Square in St. Petersburg, Russia, April 30, 2025. (AP Photo/Dmitri Lovetsky)
Peskov urged reporters to disregard other figures but offered no updated official death toll.
The investigation draws on records obtained by the hacking groups Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow after they breached Russia's federal statistics agency, Rosstat.

Researchers identified at least 490,000 registered military deaths by late September 2026. However, delays in registering fatalities and soldiers who remain officially listed as missing but are believed to be dead led researchers to estimate that the actual toll had likely reached 700,000 or more by that time.

Keti Korkiya, a research analyst at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), told Fox News Digital that she considered the estimate of more than 700,000 Russian military deaths plausible, noting that Britain's defense chief had already put the death toll above half a million in September. "The biggest uncertainty is how many of the soldiers still listed as missing have died," Korkiya said.

"Russia can keep fighting despite these losses," she added. "It still recruits tens of thousands of men a month, and this week the Duma approved a budget that devotes 35% of next year’s federal spending to defense. The war is straining Russia’s economy, but that pressure is unlikely to force Putin to stop fighting anytime soon."
UKRAINE'S ATTACKS ON RUSSIA ARE PUSHING PUTIN CLOSER TO NEGOTIATING TABLE, TRUMP NATO AMBASSADOR SAYS

In this photo taken from video distributed by Russian Defense Ministry Press Service on May 15, Russian Army soldiers prepare a 152mm howitzer Giatsint-B to fire on Ukrainian positions in Ukraine. (Russian Defense Ministry Press Service via AP)
The findings also raise questions about Russia's ability to replenish its forces nearly five years into the war.

A European intelligence source who spoke to Fox News Digital last week described Russia's efforts to replenish its forces as a form of "hidden mobilization," with recruiters approaching people on the streets, including homeless individuals, and offering them military contracts.

The source said Russia continues to recruit prisoners and target people struggling with financial difficulties, including those with outstanding debts or unpaid child support, effectively offering military service as "a kind of a social deal."
The recruitment strategy, the source said, is increasingly geared toward "more quantity, less quality."
The mounting losses have yielded limited territorial gains for Moscow, according to a separate July 1 report by the Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS).
UKRAINE HITS PUTIN'S PRIZED BRIDGE IN RECORD DRONE BLITZ AS KREMLIN TELLS LAWMAKERS TO PREPARE FOR 'VICTORY'
The launch of Ukraine’s domestically produced long-range FP-5 "Flamingo" cruise missiles during a strike on Russian military targets. (Den Shtilierman via X/East2West)
The report, authored by Seth G. Jones and Riley McCabe, estimated that Russia had suffered approximately 1.4 million battlefield casualties, including as many as 450,000 deaths, by mid-2026.

Ukraine has also suffered significant military losses. The same CSIS report estimated that between 125,000 and 150,000 Ukrainian troops had been killed between February 2022 and June 2026, with total military casualties reaching between 525,000 and 625,000.
Despite mounting military and economic pressures, the researchers warned that Putin was unlikely to abandon his ambitions in Ukraine without facing additional costs.
"Without greater costs in blood and treasure, Putin is likely to keep fighting," Jones and McCabe wrote.

Korkiya said Putin's decision to continue fighting reflects his belief that Moscow can outlast both Kyiv and its Western allies. "Putin has had opportunities to stop the fighting. When Ukraine agreed to a U.S. proposal for a 30-day ceasefire, he chose to keep fighting," she said.

"He still believes Russia can bear these losses longer than Ukraine and its allies can hold out. So far, even the deaths of hundreds of thousands of his own soldiers haven’t changed that calculation."

Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs echoed that assessment in an interview with Fox News Digital on Monday, arguing that Western leaders risk underestimating the ideological and religious beliefs driving Russia's war.
"We are too pragmatic and rational in the West," Rinkēvičs said.
RUSSIA COULD LAUNCH NUCLEAR-CAPABLE SATELLITE WITHIN WEEKS, WESTERN INTELLIGENCE WARNS: REPORT

A mother cries at the coffin of her son, Oleh Borovyk, a Ukrainian serviceman killed in fighting with Russian forces near Pokrovsk, during his funeral ceremony in Boiarka, Ukraine, on Dec. 3, 2025. (Evgeniy Maloletka/AP)

He pointed to the concept of Russia as the "Third Rome" and the belief in its historical mission to serve as the protector of Christianity, arguing that such ideological convictions also drive Moscow's foreign policy and its war against Ukraine.
"Russia is using all the diplomatic kind of decoys simply to prolong the war," Rinkēvičs said.
The Latvian president suggested that a potential diplomatic opening could emerge in the spring or summer of 2027, provided Ukraine withstands Russia's winter campaign.
"Currently, Russia explores diplomatic efforts in order to prolong the war, not to end," he said.
Meanwhile, Ukraine continues to target Russian military assets deep inside the country.

Ukraine's General Staff said Wednesday that its forces had damaged five Russian military aircraft at the Savasleyka airbase in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, including three MiG-31 fighters and two Su-34 fighter-bombers, according to an official Ukrainian military statement.
Russia did not immediately comment on the Ukrainian claims, Reuters reported Wednesday.
The ongoing fighting has also heightened concerns about the war spilling into NATO territory.

Poland's military reported Tuesday that a Russian drone had briefly entered Polish airspace during an overnight attack on western Ukraine. The incident came four days after three Russian cruise missiles landed in Poland.

title: Libyans pledge to retaliate after Ukraine strikes Russian warship near Benghazi, killing 2 soldiers
summary: The Libyan National Army mourns two soldiers who died Tuesday from a Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian warship in Benghazi, vowing retaliation.
story: Former White House official Morgan Murphy says Ukraine’s strike on Russian warship in Libya signals major shift in war.
The Libyan National Army (LNA) has vowed to retaliate after a Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship moored at a Benghazi port killed two Libyan soldiers.

"With deep sadness and sorrow, and with hearts believing in the decree and destiny of Allah, the General Command of the Libyan Arab Armed Forces mourns two of its heroic sons belonging to the Naval Forces General Staff," the LNA wrote in a Facebook post on Tuesday.
Calling the Ukrainian attack "sinful aggression," the LNA also quoted the Quran, writing, "And those who have wronged are going to know to what [kind of] return they will be returned."
RUSSIA WARNS OF 'PREVENTIVE NUCLEAR ATTACK' AS MEDVEDEV CLAIMS UKRAINE, NATO CROSSED LINE
The LNA said the soldiers, identified as Al-Taher Abdullah al-Sadiq and Lieutenant Ali Mohammed al-Said, died Tuesday from injuries sustained during the Sunday attack.

A satellite image shows a capsized and burning Russian naval ship and the northern port area after an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi naval base, which Libya's eastern-based government said was caused by a suspected drone attack, in Benghazi, Libya, November 22, 2026. (Vantor/Handout via REUTERS)

Libya's eastern government, the Government of National Stability, was joined by the country's U.N.-recognized western government, the Government of National Unity, based in the capital, Tripoli, in criticizing the attack.
US CALLS TURKEY-LIBYA MARITIME DEAL 'UNHELPFUL AND PROVOCATIVE' AMID REGIONAL BACKLASH

"The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of the Government of National Unity has expressed its condemnation and denunciation of statements made by the Ukrainian President regarding the execution of military operations targeting Russian naval vessels in the vicinity of the city of Benghazi," the Ministry wrote in a statement.
The Tripoli-based government also denied accusations that the Ukrainian attack was launched from Libyan territorial waters.
FRENCH TROOPS SECRETLY DEPLOYED INSIDE UKRAINE AS EX-NATO CHIEF PRAISES MACRON'S 'GUTS'
"The Ministry categorically rejects the conduct of any foreign military operations within Libyan territory or its territorial waters," it added.

Despite the denial, Libya's eastern government requested an investigation into the possibility that the drone strike was launched from Western Libya, citing information that Ukrainian military could be present in "areas around Misrata, Zawiya and other potential locations," according to news outlet Al Arabiya.
NATO FIGHTER JET CLEARED TO SHOOT DOWN RUSSIAN MISSILE OVER POLAND AS WARSAW PUSHES FOR US TROOPS
Western Libya's government criticized the Benghazi-based eastern government for hosting Russian ships in the first place.
"Hosting illicit foreign forces and granting them access to national facilities invites the spillover of external conflicts into the country," Tripoli said, according to Al Arabiya.

A satellite image shows a capsized and burning Russian naval ship and the northern port area after an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi naval base, which Libya's eastern-based government said was caused by a suspected drone attack, in Benghazi, Libya, November 22, 2026. (Vantor/Handout via REUTERS)

The Benghazi-based LNA is the military arm of Libya's eastern government, one half of the ruling party in the North African nation. Following the fall of former Libyan dictator Muammar Qadaffi, rivaling power factions made claims on ruling the nation.
The United Nations-backed western government counts the U.S. and European Union among its supporters. The eastern government is broadly aligned with Russia and is not formally recognized by the U.N.
Russia supported Libya's vow for revenge.
"Well, certainly, no state will leave an attempt on the lives of its servicemen unpunished," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said in a video.

Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov moderates Russian President Vladimir Putin's annual special televised question-and-answer session and year-end news conference, held at the Gostiny Dvor trade and exhibition center in Moscow, Russia, on December 19, 2025. (Sefa Karacan/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Ukraine, while confirming the strike, claimed it was self-defense.

"Ukraine respects the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Libya. We emphasize that Ukraine's actions are aimed at countering Russian armed aggression and are not intended to harm Libya or its people," Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said in a message posted to Telegram.

Sybiha also said that the ships it attacked — Russian naval vessels and cargo ships transporting military equipment — were valid military targets as defined by the United Nations Charter's Article 51.
"Ukraine is not 'dragging' anyone into the war or 'transferring' the war anywhere," Sybiha added.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also confirmed a separate drone strike on a Russian ship in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday.

title: Christians increasingly targeted across Europe as watchdog warns of rising hostility
summary: Anti-Christian hate crimes in Europe rose 44% last year, says the Vienna observatory, which documented 2,465 incidents in 2025 across the continent.
story: Lord Stewart Jackson alleges ‘two-tier justice’ allows Islamist extremists to preach while Christian pastors face harassment.
Attacks targeting Christians across Europe rose 44% last year, according to a new report from the Vienna-based Observatory on Intolerance and Discrimination Against Christians in Europe (OIDAC).
Their research documented 2,465 anti-Christian hate crimes and incidents in 2025, with France, England and Wales, Germany and Austria recording the highest totals.

"Our primary concern with the new data is that anti-Christian attacks that target persons, individuals themselves, have risen," OIDAC executive director Anja Tang told Fox News Digital. "Clergy and people responsible for places of worship were those who were most attacked and also where numbers increased most strongly."
CHRISTIAN WOMAN PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO NEW 'ORWELLIAN' CHARGES FOR STANDING AND SILENT PRAYER
Christian cross against the sky. (Godong/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

She added, "These would be people who were present, were visible, recognizable as Christians and kind of associated with a church." Tang noted that while OIDAC’s numbers are "quite conservative," saying "aggression against individuals is highly underreported" across Europe.

The group said French authorities recorded a 70% increase in attacks on individuals, the highest in Europe, although Tang notes the French government has not yet published a detailed explanation of the increase. OIDAC argues the increase in attacks against individuals warrants separate attention from incidents involving vandalism, theft and arson targeting religious property.

The findings come as the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) has begun highlighting anti-Christian hate crimes through a dedicated practical guide, and amid debate over whether attacks on Christians receive the same public attention as incidents targeting other religious communities. Tang said OIDAC is one of the largest contributors of anti-Christian hate-crime data to the OSCE's reporting system, and OIDAC uses the OSCE’s methodology when classifying incidents.
WORLD-FAMOUS CATHOLIC SHRINE TORCHED, 'DEVIL IN A SKIRT' SCRAWLED ON VIRGIN MARY STATUE

Police were first called around 4:30 a.m. on July 27 after the face and hands of the statue of the Virgin Mary on Apparition Hill, also known as Podbrdo, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, were found covered in black paint. (Associated Press)

The findings have also drawn concern from Alessandro Calcagno, deputy general secretary of the Commission of the Bishops’ Conferences of the EU (COMECE) and advisor on fundamental rights and freedom of religion within the EU. In a statement to Fox News Digital, Calcagno says "the vital and courageous work constantly carried out by" OIDAC "underscores the importance of EU mechanisms to counter a phenomenon that does exist in Europe and that therefore cannot be ignored at the institutional and policy level."

Lorenzo Vidino, director of the Program on Extremism at George Washington University, says anti-Christian incidents appear to stem from a mix of sources, including anti-religious activists, some individuals from Muslim backgrounds and ordinary vandalism.

Vidino said anti-Christian attacks often receive less public attention than similar incidents involving other faith groups. "There's no question there's been acts of violence against Muslims, against Jews and that's despicable. And when it happens, it is prosecuted," he tells Fox News Digital. "When the same act happens against churches or Christian sites, it doesn't happen in the same way."
STATE DEPARTMENT PRESSES EGYPT TO RESPECT RELIGIOUS FREEDOM AS CHRISTIAN CONVERT FACES POSSIBLE EXECUTION

French police officers stand near Notre Dame in Nice, southern France, Oct. 29, 2020. French President Emmanuel Macron has announced that he will more than double number of soldiers deployed to protect against attacks to 7,000 after three people were killed at a church Thursday. (Eric Gaillard/Pool via AP)
"While the law might be neutral, the common perception of things is not neutral, and so those incidents are not prioritized," he said.

Calcagno says protecting places of worship "cannot be reduced to acts of terrorism, but should also cover other types of attacks against them," including vandalism, violence, profanation, disruptions of religious services, arson and harassment.

Tang said OIDAC is also concerned about migrant communities, including Christians fleeing persecution in the Middle East and asylum seekers "who have left Islam behind and are really facing quite severe aggression because of their choice of religion." She notes these groups "really need protection," and that most incidents involving these groups go unreported "out of fear of stigmatization."

Tang said she was surprised by the number of attacks "connected to pro-life convictions" and carried out by "left-wing extremist groups" that OIDAC categorized as anti-Christian incidents in German-speaking Europe, noting "the level of this violence was just significantly more than what I have seen in my time observing these trends."
CARRYING A BIBLE IN NORTHERN IRELAND HOSPITALS COULD BE A CRIME UNDER ABORTION BUFFER ZONE LAWS

Forensic police officers inspect the scene of a knife attack at Notre Dame church in Nice, southern France, Oct. 29, 2020. An attacker armed with a knife killed three people at a church in Nice, prompting the prime minister to announce that France was raising its security alert status to the highest level. (Eric Gaillard/Pool via AP)

She pointed to a café run by a Leipzig, Germany, church that was forced to close its doors after being vandalized over 26 times because of "their Christian worldview," and an Austrian church that was forced to evacuate in the middle of holy Mass due to "a fake bomb being placed there by left-wing groups… because it was a prayer connected to a pro-life event."
She said,"I find it shocking the level of violence that's often shown by groups who disagree, who plead for tolerance, but then themselves behave the most intolerant."

Calcagno backs OIDAC's call for a dedicated EU coordinator on combating anti-Christian hatred, a position COMECE has repeatedly requested and one it "hopes that the European Commission will take up in the near future." He stressed that such a role would complement existing EU coordinators addressing antisemitism and anti-Muslim hatred, positions that he said "rightly exist at the EU level."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

OIDAC is urging European governments to adopt recommendations contained in the OSCE's recent practical guide on anti-Christian hate crimes, including improving the recording of incidents, strengthening prevention efforts and expanding support for victims. The group also renewed its call for the EU to appoint a coordinator dedicated to combating anti-Christian hatred.

Tyler Speicher is an American journalist living in Slovenia after spending 25 years covering stories ranging from the Little League World Series to hurricanes, 9/11 and its aftermath for New York City news outlets, including 20 years on the Fox News Channel assignment desk.

title: Yemeni military official brands Iran Houthis’ ‘godfather,’ says Tehran is directing war
summary: Yemeni armed forces say Iran's IRGC and Hezbollah experts are directing Houthis' missile, drone and naval attacks on shipping near Bab el-Mandeb.
story: A deadly missile attack on Yemen's presidential palace by Iran-backed Houthis kills two security guards and threatens Saudi airspace. Fox News' Trey Yingst reports on escalating Middle East tensions as Iran prepares for war.

Yemen’s military is vowing to defeat the Iran-backed Houthis and retake one of the world’s most strategic maritime choke points, warning that Tehran is directly involved in the planning and execution of a war with implications far beyond Yemen’s borders.

In an on-the-record briefing Tuesday attended by Fox News Digital, Col. Majed Abdullah Al-Nuzaily, the official spokesperson for the Yemeni Armed Forces, acknowledged recent military setbacks but insisted that government forces were prepared to counter the Houthi offensive.

"This is not a conventional battle against an isolated local armed group," Al-Nuzaily said. "What we have seen on the battlefield proves that we are not facing the Houthis alone. This is an Iranian battle: Iranian in its weapons, in its planning and command, and in its direction and timing."
RUBIO ACCUSES IRAN OF FLYING IRGC PERSONNEL INTO YEMEN AS HOUTHI THREAT ESCALATES

Members of the Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces react during what they say to be clashes with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis in a location given as near as Al-Hazm, Yemen, in this screen grab obtained from a handout video released September 9, 2026. (Media Centre Of The Yemeni Armed Forces/Handout via Reuters)

The colonel said external supply networks had provided the Houthis with ballistic and cruise missiles, sophisticated drones and advanced electronic warfare capabilities, enabling the group to threaten neighboring countries and international shipping. "Iran is the Houthis' patron, their godfather," he said.

Al-Nuzaily said Yemen’s Interior Ministry had identified 21 foreign experts working with the Houthis, including 14 from Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and seven from Hezbollah, allegedly assisting with missile and drone operations, naval attacks and the selection of commercial ships to target. "And we have the evidence to prove it," he said.

The briefing comes as Yemeni government forces face mounting pressure from the Houthis, who, according to Al-Nuzaily, now control the coastline along the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and Mayyun Island, which sits in the middle of the strategic waterway connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.
HOUTHIS ENTER US 'KILL BOX' AFTER SEIZING RED SEA 'CORK,' FORMER PENTAGON OFFICIAL WARNS

Satellite imagery shows Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping waterway and the gateway to the Red Sea, as Iran threatens using Yemen's Houthi allies to shut the Bab el-Mandeb gateway to the Red Sea, in this handout picture dated July 12, 2026. (NASA Worldview/Handout via Reuters)
"Bab el-Mandeb remains a priority. We retook it once in a matter of days. We will retake it again, and next time we will hold the mountains as well as the shore," he said.
Al-Nuzaily warned that Tehran views the waterway as a source of leverage against Washington.

"Control of Bab el-Mandeb is at the heart of Iran's strategy. Together with the Strait of Hormuz, it gives Tehran another card to play in its confrontation with the United States, and a way to improve its terms at the negotiating table."

But Yemeni officials warned that the Houthis are increasingly developing their own transnational terrorist network, including cooperation with Somalia-based al-Shabab, meaning a potential agreement between Washington and Tehran would not necessarily eliminate the threat.
NEW RISK FOR US CONSUMERS AS IRAN-BACKED ATTACKS THREATEN A SECOND MAJOR OIL CHOKEPOINT
Houthi supporters chant slogans during an anti-U.S. and anti-Israel rally in Sanaa, Yemen, Monday, March 17, 2025. (AP Photo/Osamah Abdulrahman)
"When ISIS paraded a single missile, the world trembled – and took action. Today, the Houthis have thousands of ballistic and cruise missiles," Al-Nuzaily said.

Ambassador Marwan Ali Al Noman, political adviser to Yemen’s minister of foreign affairs, expressed gratitude for the Trump administration’s support and the U.S. designation of the Houthis as a terrorist organization, while calling for greater international assistance.
"We are not asking anyone to fight this war for us," Al Noman said. "We are asking for partners."
SAUDI ARABIA TELLS TRUMP NOW IS THE TIME FOR MILITARY ACTION AS IRAN-BACKED HOUTHIS ADVANCE
Houthi supporters demonstrate in solidarity with Iran, amid a two-week ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran, in Sanaa, Yemen, April 10, 2026. (Khaled Abdullah/Reuters)
He said Yemen was seeking military equipment, training, coast guard assistance and expanded sanctions against networks supplying the Houthis with weapons and financing.
Yemen launched Operation Dawn of Yemen on Oct. 4 with the stated objectives of restoring state institutions, retaking the capital, Sanaa, and ending Houthi rule.

Government forces have since faced setbacks, including a withdrawal from the Bab el-Mandeb earlier this month. Al-Nuzaily acknowledged that Houthi forces were approximately 37 miles from Aden, the seat of Yemen’s government, but insisted the city was secure and that military forces now operate under a unified command.
"Some say this war cannot be won," Al-Nuzaily said. "I say to them: you do not know the Yemeni people."

"For 12 years, they have been told to accept the Houthis. For 12 years, they have refused. They have buried their sons and kept fighting. They have lost their homes and kept fighting. They will not kneel to men who rule by fear, who send children to die and who answer to Tehran rather than to Yemen."

Protesters hold weapons during a demonstration of predominantly Houthi supporters to show solidarity with Palestinians in the Gaza Strip and to condemn U.S. strikes in Yemen, in Sanaa, Yemen, May 30, 2025. (REUTERS/Adel Al Khader)
"Dawn has come to Yemen. It will not be turned back."
