title: Too young to be vaccinated for measles? Babies face growing threats from outbreaks
summary: As measles outbreaks continue to soar, a new question has emerged: Should doctors give measles shots earlier to better protect babies?
story: As measles outbreaks continue to soar nationwide, increasingly spilling from small, close-knit communities into the general population, a new question has emerged: Should doctors give measles shots earlier to better protect babies?

Dr. Kristen Panthagani, an emergency medicine doctor in Connecticut, is worried about her baby, who has just turned 6 months old — too young for the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine that’s given after age 1.

“I’ve been trying to figure out what to do to protect my son,” Panthagani said on her public health blog, called “You can know things.” He’s “in a tricky period when it comes to measles. He’s in a window of vulnerability where he likely doesn’t have protection against the virus.”
Babies are born with antibodies against measles if their mothers have been vaccinated. But new evidence shows that protection doesn’t last as long as previously thought.

“The assumption has always been that up until 6 months of age, babies are protected, and then from 6 to 12 months, there’s some waning,” said Dr. Buddy Creech, a pediatric infectious disease specialist and director of the Vanderbilt Vaccine Research Program at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. “That’s why we give the vaccine at 12 months.”

New research from Creech’s team shows that protection is gone long before a child’s first birthday. Researchers analyzed blood samples from 92 mother-infant pairs and found that less than 20% of 6-month-old babies still have those protective antibodies.

“By somewhere between 4 to 6 months of age, the majority of kids have completely lost the level of seroprotection that would be needed to protect against measles,” Creech said. He presented the research at an October meeting of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. It’s not been peer-reviewed.
For more on the measles outbreak, read The Vaccine Divide, a data investigation into how the deadly virus is roaring back and childhood vaccine defenses continue to crack and crumble.
Now that cases have exploded in the U.S., babies in that 6- to 11-month window are increasingly defenseless against the virus.
“We’re going to have to rethink when we should give the first dose of measles vaccine,” Creech said.
When should kids get their measles shots?

For decades, the guidance was straightforward: Children receive their first MMR shot at 12 to 15 months old, followed by a second dose between ages 4 and 6. Together, the shots are 97% effective at protecting against measles, usually for life.
In areas with active outbreaks, however, babies at 6 months old can get an early or “zero” MMR shot ahead of their two regular doses.
And toddlers who’ve already had their first regular dose don’t have to wait until age 4 for their second shot. They’re eligible for the second dose 28 days after their first for maximum protection.

Many parents in outbreak areas have taken advantage of the change in guidance. “We have seen huge uptake in the zero dose as well as in the early second dose,” Pennsylvania Secretary of Health Dr. Debra Bogen said last week during a briefing with the Association of State and Territorial Health Officials. More than 67,000 early MMR shots have been given in Pennsylvania since July, according to the state health department.

The growing question now is whether those exceptions should become more widely used — or whether the routine vaccination schedule itself needs reconsideration — now that the U.S. has lost its measles elimination status.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

“There are people looking at this right now. They’re reviewing all of the latest science and seeing if the recommendation should change,” said Dr. Deanna Behrens, a Chicago-area pediatrician and secretary of the Illinois chapter of the American Academy of Pediatrics. “We are on high alert.”

As of Friday, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention had confirmed 5,838 cases, though the number is likely a vast undercount. More than 1,000 of those cases have been in kids under 5. About 17% of those children have needed hospitalization.

Most kids recover from measles without a problem. But as the virus has caught fire across the U.S., doctors in outbreak zones have reported severe complications in some children, including trouble breathing, severe dehydration, pneumonia and brain swelling. Babies with measles are also at greater risk of developing a condition called subacute sclerosing panencephalitis, or SSPE, years after their infection. It’s almost always fatal.
Twelve people have died of measles this year, according to state health departments. At least half of those deaths have been in babies or toddlers.

The Vaccine Integrity Project, part of the University of Minnesota’s Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy, recently summarized the latest data on zero doses of MMR vaccine. The shot is 58% effective when given between 6 and 9 months, and 83% between 9 and 11 months.
Side effects from the shots, such as fever and, rarely, febrile seizures, were the same in younger and older children.
But there’s also evidence, the Vaccine Integrity Project’s review found, that the zero dose may impact how well kids’ immune systems respond to the two routinely recommended MMR shots.

“It’s a trade-off right now,” said Dr. Heidi Moline, a pediatrician and clinical adviser to the Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy. “When there’s a significant amount of measles virus circulating, the short-term benefit of protection against measles outweighs the long-term lower antibodies.”

As of now, there’s no indication the CDC is considering changes to the childhood vaccine schedule. The AAP said the group will review all of its immunization recommendations early next year. The CDC didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

Vaccines recommended by the CDC’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices are generally free. There have been reports of health insurance claims being denied for early MMR vaccination, according to the AAP.
“This is something the vaccine policy people are really going to have to look at,” said Dr. Peter Hotez, co-director of the Texas Children’s Hospital Center for Vaccine Development.

title: Judge halts order requiring Fulton County to turn over copies of 2020 ballots
summary: The judge previously ruled the county had to turn over unredacted digital copies of election materials to the State Election Board, which is run by Trump allies.
story: A Fulton County judge on Wednesday paused her own order from a day before that had required the county to hand over digital copies of its 2020 election records to the Georgia State Election Board.

Superior Court Judge Kelly Lee Ellerbe halted the previous day’s order while the appeal from the county plays out. The move by Ellerbe, who issued a one-page ruling that did not elaborate on her reasoning, came hours before the 5 p.m. ET deadline to hand over records to the election board, which is controlled by allies of President Donald Trump.

Atlanta’s Fulton County, which is the home of a large chunk of the state’s Democratic voters, has long been a target of Trump and his allies as they seek to find evidence to support their false claims of widespread voter fraud in the 2020 election won by former President Joe Biden.
For Subscribers

The records at the heart of the Georgia case are unredacted digital copies of 2020 election materials, the originals of which were seized from the county’s elections hub in January by the FBI in an unusual federal intervention into a state-run election.
For Subscribers
The judge said Tuesday that the records could only be disclosed to a limited number of parties outlined in the order.
The board has been trying to obtain the records since 2024.

title: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade pushed back to Saturday due to weather
summary: Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day parade will be pushed back to Saturday because of severe weather, officials said.
story: Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day parade will be pushed back to Saturday because of severe weather, officials said.

“The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration,” Macy’s said Wednesday.
The parade will now kick off at 8:30 a.m. ET Saturday.
“Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year. We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday,” Macy’s said.
The postponement came as the East Coast was bracing to be hit by stormy weather on Thanksgiving Day, bringing heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding, according to the National Weather Service.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a news conference Wednesday evening that New Yorkers will see a heavy storm Thursday, with forecast sustained winds between 30 and 40 mph and possible gusts as high as 65 mph. The National Weather Service has issued a high wind warning and coastal flood warning for parts of New York on Thanksgiving Day.
The mayor warned winds will be strong enough to down tree limbs and power lines.

“If you are traveling, please budget extra time and use caution. Leave early and prepare for the possibility that you may have to stay late. There is no destination worth risking your safety. If conditions become severe, please stay indoors and wait until it is safe to travel,” he said.

Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade executive producer Will Coss said Wednesday that while the team is “heartbroken” to postpone the parade, “the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants and spectators, is, and always will be, our top priority.”
He said the balloons currently in New York will have to be taken down and transported to a facility in New Jersey.

“They have to go back and be parade readied again, so they have to be prepared, which is a weeks-long process that’s going to get condensed to about 24 hours,” Coss explained. “The team is going to be hard at work preparing for Saturday. So by the time we’re ready to deliver back to New York City, it’s really about inflating and getting ourselves stepped off for a successful parade.”

New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said police are working closely with Macy’s and other officials on a comprehensive security plan for the parade, and so far there’s “no specific, credible threats to the parade at this time.”
Since its debut in 1924, the parade has only been cancelled three times — in 1942, 1943 and 1944 — because materials for giant balloons were needed for the World War II effort.
Balloons were last grounded in 1971 due to fierce winds and rain. City regulations mandate balloons can’t fly if sustained winds exceed 23 mph.

The historic parade, which marches from the Upper West Side to Macy’s Herald Square flagship store, is set to feature performers from nine Broadway shows, 100 balloons and inflatables, and a slate of beloved floats including Bugs Bunny, Curious George and Scooby-Doo.
NBC said it will air last year’s Thanksgiving Day parade at 8:30 a.m. Thursday in all time zones, and Saturday’s parade will be broadcast at 8:30 that morning.

title: Steelers cut Aaron Rodgers after he blasts coach Mike McCarthy in fiery exit interview
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers released quarterback Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday shortly after he described his head coach Mike McCarthy as “unhealthy” in a critical interview following the Steelers’ decision to deactivate Rodgers for the team’s upcoming game.
story: The Pittsburgh Steelers released quarterback Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday shortly after he described his head coach Mike McCarthy as “unhealthy” in a critical interview following the Steelers’ decision to deactivate Rodgers for the team’s upcoming game.
Speaking to ESPN’s Pat McAfee on Wednesday, Rodgers accused McCarthy of falling asleep during team meetings and missing walk-throughs in the weeks leading up to his benching.

“Last Thursday, I was in a quarterback meeting and in 10 minutes I heard snoring,” Rodgers said of his head coach. “Thursday, he misses an offensive meeting. Friday, he misses walk-through... Saturday, he misses the team meeting.”
Added Rodgers: “If you’re sleeping in meetings, you’re unhealthy.”
Following the interview, the team announced Rodgers had been released.
The Steelers are 6-4 and have lost their last two games. On Tuesday night, the team announced that Rodgers would be inactive for the team’s game Friday against the Denver Broncos.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The Steelers did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Rodgers’ interview.

Rodgers blasted McCarthy while speaking to McAfee, alleging his coach even broke down a team huddle with a “one, two, three, Packers!” last week, confusing players. (McCarthy was previously Rodgers’ coach in Green Bay from 2006 to 2018.)
“Everybody knows what’s going on. He’s missing walk-throughs, you don’t think everybody else knows?” Rodgers said. “Does any other quarterback have these issues?”
Rodgers added: “It’s a very delicate situation, the coaching staff is worried about their job security, the players are worried about their money and jobs security.”
Rodgers said he is willing to speak out about McCarthy because of the financial security his long career has afforded him.
Rodgers also said McCarthy hasn’t connected with Pittsburgh’s defense, and rebuffed Rodgers’ efforts to get him to connect with players on that side of the ball.
Rodgers also said McCarthy has not been watching film and lacks an intimate knowledge of the team’s week-to-week game plans.
“I don’t expect people to come out strong in my defense even though everybody knows the truth,” the quarterback said.
Rodgers said issues with McCarthy began in training camp, and he also accused his coach of harboring ill will over his dismissal from the Packers.
“In Mike’s mind, I got him fired in 2018. He told a staff member he still doesn’t forgive me for getting him fired in 2018,” Rodgers said.

In the hours before his benching, Rodgers said he brought up his issues with McCarthy in an in-person conversation and delivered him an ultimatum to either address the problems or grant him a release. Rodgers said McCarthy did not admit to sleeping during team meetings, and the idea of his benching was not raised.
“I found out that I was going to be inactive on a phone call last night from Pat Freiermuth,” Rodgers said, referring to the tight end.
The quarterback repeatedly said his stories are not “hyperbole” or “opinion,” but instead firsthand accounts and facts.

Rodgers, 42, has said on several occasions the 2026 season would be his final one in the NFL. A four-time MVP and a former Super Bowl champion, Rodgers in recent years has become equally notable for his willingness to speak freely, opining on topics from the Covid vaccine to the benefits he feels of taking psychedelic drugs.
Rodgers is also a frequent guest on McAfee’s ESPN show, and was previously paid for weekly appearances on the program.

As he’s become a lightning rod for his public comments, Rodgers’ play on the field has slipped in the late stage of his career. He’s averaging a career-low 6.2 yards per attempt this season, and Rodgers has not posted a passer rating higher than 95.0 in five seasons after doing so 12 times between 2008 and 2021.

McCarthy spoke with reporters at a news conference in the wake of Rodgers’ comments, and refuted multiple claims. McCarthy said it was “not accurate” that he held a grudge with Rodgers over his firing in 2018, and also said he made multiple attempts to reach Rodgers to inform him of his benching.
But the coach also largely avoided getting into the finer details of Rodgers’ accusations.
“We are focused on beating Denver,” McCarthy said.

title: Mississippi plane crash victims were members of a Florida family returning from a fishing trip
summary: A deadly plane crash off the coast of Mississippi claimed the lives of six members of a southwest Florida family who were flying home from Louisiana after a fishing trip, officials confirmed Wednesday.
story: A deadly plane crash off the coast of Mississippi claimed the lives of six members of a southwest Florida family who were flying home from Louisiana after a fishing trip, officials confirmed Wednesday.

They were identified as Brent Stokes, 50, Michael Knox, 43, Arlyn Knox, 43, Charles Holden Knox, 12, Truett Knox, 10, and Hunter Stokes, 16. The names were confirmed by the plane’s owner, Rhonda Culmer.
They all lived in Fort Myers, Florida, records show.

“They died doing what they loved: celebrating the start of a wonderful holiday season with a fishing trip together, before heading home to be with the rest of our family,” the family said in a statement obtained by NBC affiliate WBBH-TV. “In the middle of our grief, we are holding on to that, and to how much love they gave us and how much love surrounds us now. We will carry them with us always.”
The plane was piloted by Brent Stokes, according to WBBH-TV.

Stokes, according to available records, is president of a Fort Myers marine construction company called Stokes Marine. He was the father of Hunter Stokes, according to Bruce Lynd Jr., the Jackson County, Mississippi, coroner.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Stokes was also the brother of Arlyn Knox, who ran a local IT company with her husband, Michael Knox, called Knox Technology. Charles and Truett were their sons, the coroner said.
Knox Technology declined to comment.

The family had been in Louisiana on a fishing trip and was flying home to Fort Myers. Their single-engine Cesna took off from New Orleans Lakefront Airport about 2 p.m. local time on Tuesday, officials said.
The plane went down around 3:30 p.m. some two 2 miles northeast of Horn Island, the Coast Guard said.
“That’s when they lost communication,” said Juan Ros, a Coast Guard public affairs officer, adding that radar showed the plane descending “at 10,000 feet per minute.”
Divers from the Mississippi Department of Marine Resources found the victims in the plane’s fuselage, the Coast Guard’s Heartland District office in New Orleans said in a statement Tuesday night.
The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating the crash.

“We are deeply grateful to the U.S. Coast Guard, the Mississippi Department of Marine Resources, and everyone who searched for and brought our family home,” the family said in its statement. “We also thank everyone who has reached out with prayers and kindness.”
Photos from Arlyn Knox’s Facebook account show that the family appeared to share a love of sports and traveling.

The pictures show the Knox children, Charles Holden Knox and Truett Knox, playing in local soccer, baseball and basketball little leagues. The family also seemed to root for the University of Florida Gators, according to images.
The family took trips to the Bahamas, the mountains of North Carolina and Savannah, Georgia last summer, according to the account.

In January, Arlyn Knox shared photos of her and her husband, Michael Knox, in honor of their 12th wedding anniversary. The photos show the young couple posing by a body of water and kissing under fireworks.
In December 2023, Arlyn Knox posted several photos appearing to show her Michael Knox in the cockpit of a small plane with her two children.
“One year ago he said he wanted to become a pilot, and today he passed his check ride!!” she wrote. “We love you!”

title: A rising political star in China is the latest victim of Xi’s purge
summary: He was on the rise among China’s political elite, hosting tech leaders and senior American officials.
story: He was on the rise among China’s political elite, hosting tech leaders and senior American officials. But now Shanghai party chief Chen Jining, a member of the country’s influential politburo, appears to be the latest senior official brought down by President Xi Jinping’s sweeping purge.

The hammer unexpectedly came down on Chen in the form of a two-line bulletin on the Xinhua news agency Tuesday: He is “suspected of serious violations of Party discipline and law and is currently under disciplinary review and supervisory investigation” — a common euphemism for corruption crackdowns on ruling Communist Party officials under Xi.
Public announcements such as these usually mark the end of a political career in China. Chen has made no public statement.

He is the fourth politburo member to be purged in less than two years, part of a broader crackdown that has swept aside top military leaders as Xi consolidates power. He is set to extend his rule next year, at a party congress that is held once every five years and looms over the preceding months.
But Chen’s abrupt downfall took many close observers of China by surprise, given his profile and career path would usually point to a bright future.

“He was potentially going to the highest level, which would be the standing committee. And I think from a lot of Western observers, people thought he had even better prospects,” Damien Ma, the Singapore-based director of the Carnegie China think tank, told NBC News.
Xi’s pursuit of loyalty

Some analysts have speculated that Xi, increasingly viewed as likely to rule for life, may have been purging a viable replacement. Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London, said however that Chen was “someone who could rise further but not as a successor.”

Chen, a 62-year-old technocrat known as a friend of foreign business and an advocate for AI, was an environmental scientist who studied in London and swiftly rose through the party’s ranks. He served as China’s environmental minister, Beijing’s mayor and the party secretary in Shanghai — a post once held by Xi and widely considered a stepping stone to bigger things.

Just last month, Chen hosted Apple Chairman Tim Cook, welcoming the U.S. tech giant to “make full use of Shanghai’s strengths” and bring more products to the city, a financial and cultural hub that has long served as a connection between China and the international community.
In his last public appearance last week, during a tour of a shipping facility, Chen called for advancing the industry’s digital transformation.
By Wednesday, Chen’s name has been removed from some official websites. A webpage on the Shanghai government site showing that meeting with Cook is now showing a 404 message, or not found.

Chen is just the latest senior official in the crosshairs of Xi’s long-running anti-corruption campaign and emphasis on party discipline, which analysts say is as much about loyalty as it is about reform.

“It is a warning to all technocrats, as Chen was a rising star among technocrats and had no apparent failures in a technocratic way. So, message is: adhere to strict party discipline and demonstrate unquestionable loyalty to Xi or else,” Tsang said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The party’s Central Committee, which has about 200 mostly male leaders, vowed to “ensure more rigorous discipline enforcement, and make full use of discipline as a guide, restraint, guarantee, and incentive” at its closed-door gathering, the fifth plenum, last month.

“What they’ve been building as part of this discipline machine over the last 15 years is to kind of implement their sort of internal operating system of how they deal with, let’s say, bad eggs within the party,” Ma, of Carnegie China, said.

“The top leadership is normalizing this anti-corruption, this self-cleansing,” Ma said. “It is now a normal part of what the party expects, and they’re trying to embed that over time and down to every single level,” he added.

The Chinese government has not announced any charges against Chen, who was the youngest member of the country’s elite decision-making body. The 24-member Politburo was unveiled in 2022 but is now down to 21 members after the purges. Last month, top general Zhang Shengmin was elevated to the body in a rare addition.

Chen’s undoing comes a year before the party’s top leadership is reshuffled at the 21st Communist Party Congress, when Xi is expected to solidify control even further and cement another five-year term at the helm of the country.
From London to Shanghai

Born in 1964, Chen studied at the prestigious Tsinghua university, long a major pipeline for senior party officials and where he served as president from 2012 to 2015. His name has now been removed from Tsinghua’s online list of former presidents.
After studying at Tsinghua in the 1980s, he moved for a decade to Britain, where he obtained a doctorate from Imperial College London in 1993.
Chen returned to Tsinghua’s environmental science and engineering department in 1998 before being named the university’s president in 2012, according to an official biography.
He’s authored dozens of papers, including on carbon emission reduction and water quality monitoring.

The relatively young Chen would ride around campus on his bike and built a reputation for pushing institutional reforms in his three years at the helm of the university, according to an article in People’s Digest, a magazine affiliated with the People’s Daily, the community party’s official newspaper.

The article, titled “From University President to Cabinet Minister,” was published in 2015, the same year he was picked to lead the Environmental Protection Ministry. In 2017, Chen became mayor of the capital, Beijing, where he oversaw the 2022 Winter Olympics during the Covid pandemic.

title: Markets sell-off eases up, but AI doubts, tariffs and inflation still weigh down stocks
summary: U.S. stocks declined Wednesday in a volatile day of trading that was led by companies linked to the AI boom.
story: U.S. stocks declined Wednesday in a volatile day of trading that was led by companies linked to the AI boom.
From the outset, markets faced a rare combination of new inflation data, a tariff announcement from the White House and lingering concerns about the strength of the AI economy.
A sharp sell-off in the morning briefly sent the Nasdaq 100 index down more than 20% from its most recent high, before sentiment improved slightly.
Major indexes ultimately closed well off their worst levels of the day.

The Nasdaq Composite and Nasdaq 100 both ended the day lower by only 0.6% and the S&P 500 wrapped up the day lower by just 0.2%. The Dow end the trading day, slightly above the symbolic 50,000 level, up 164 points.
One beneficiary of that renewed optimism was Anthropic, the AI giant that staged a record-setting IPO last week, only to see its stock battered for three straight trading sessions.
Anthropic’s stock traded in positive territory at several points throughout the day, but still closed just shy of its $83 IPO price.
Stocks Wednesday likely faced additional pressure due to the looming Thanksgiving holiday.
U.S. markets will be closed Thursday and open for only a half-day of trading Friday.
Investors are more likely to cut their large or risky trades before extended weekends, in order to avoid being trapped in positions while events unfold.
Nvidia lags behind

Even as markets pulled back from their lows, Nvidia remained among the biggest losers in key indexes. After soaring by 31% on Monday on news that its recently-departed CEO Jensen Huang would return to the C-suite, the stock ended lower by 3.9% Wednesday, its second straight down day.
For Subscribers

The return of Huang, a de facto ambassador for the artificial intelligence industry, briefly reassured investors that big AI firms, and the trillions of dollars they borrow and lend, would continue to grow without interruption.
Stock markets Monday staged their biggest one-day rally since April 2025, as the Nasdaq 100 skyrocketed 6.8% and the S&P 500 surged 4.7%.

President Donald Trump pushed Nvidia’s board to reinstate Huang over the weekend despite multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy. Before the president stepped in, the board had been unequivocal that it did not plan to reinstate Huang.

Trump said Monday that he “probably” decided to intervene in Nvidia’s internal leadership decision because he was concerned about a market sell-off in the week after Huang’s departure fueled partly by investor concerns about how the CEO’s resignation would impact the broader AI industry.
But ever since Monday’s rally, markets have struggled to maintain that upward momentum.
“The risk-off tone has returned over the last 24 hours, as Monday’s rebound in tech stocks lost momentum once again,” Deutsche Bank strategists said in a note early Wednesday.

Before Monday’s one-day rally, stocks had faced weeks of selling, which pushed the Nasdaq 100 into correction territory on Friday, which is defined as a 10% drop from its last high. It remains in correction territory as of Wednesday’s closing bell.

Shares of semiconductor stocks, as tracked by the Philadelphia semiconductor index, have plunged more than 40% since their last peak in June. Stocks of companies that make data center and computer memory products have plummeted 60% over the same period.
New tariffs fuel uncertainty
On top of cracks in the AI sector, “matters weren’t helped by the latest tariff headlines,” Deutsche Bank’s team wrote.
For Subscribers
On Wednesday, the Trump administration unveiled a new wave of tariffs on the United States’ top trading partners, such as the European Union, China, Japan and a dozen more.

“It is another reminder that while the legal justification for tariffs keeps changing, US protectionism is becoming increasingly difficult to unwind,” ING senior trade economist Inga Fechner wrote in a note Wednesday.

That drove stocks down further, with the prospect that more tariffs could cause renewed trade tensions, a renewed inflation spike and cause a flare-up with a policy that had largely started to subside in recent months.

Even before Wednesday’s formal announcement, a spokesperson for the Chinese Commerce Ministry blasted the new import duties. “Tariff wars and trade wars are in the interests of neither side,” the spokesperson said. The ministry called it “political manipulation.”

“Some investors might have been caught off guard by news that the Administration is on track to release more tariffs, but the key question about the Administration unveiling new tariffs from the Section 301 overcapacity investigation has never been an issue of whether but when,” wrote Sarah Bianchi, chief strategist of international political affairs at Evercore ISI.
Inflation is still climbing
Compounding the negative pressure facing investors Wednesday, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge moved further away from its 2% goal.

The personal consumption expenditures index was 3.8% for October, up from 3.6% in September. Even excluding food and energy, the “core” inflation reading rose to 3.3%. It had been 3.1% the previous month.
The rise in core inflation readings is particularly noteworthy because it can indicate that higher gas prices sparked by the Iran war are spilling over into the rest of the economy.
It also raises the likelihood that the Fed will raise interest rates at its next meeting, which concludes with a rate decision Dec. 9.
Last week, a top Fed policymaker said the central bank needed to “shock people” with a larger rate hike than is typical.
“I’m very, very concerned about inflation,” Fed governor Christopher Waller said in a CNBC interview. “It’s kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out.”
Waller said the Fed needed to take “more aggressive actions,” such as hiking by 0.50%, more than the Fed’s usual 0.25% rate increase. “You might need to, like, shock people,” he said.

A rate hike would carry its own complications, however. As trillion-dollar tech giants borrow hundreds of billions of dollars to build out AI data centers and chips, any increase to interest rates could quickly raise their massive costs.

It could also hurt an already pained U.S. consumer. Mortgage rates continue to hover well above 7%, and a rate hike could push borrowing costs higher for auto loans, credit cards, personal loans and other forms of credit.

title: More than 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war, new estimate suggests
summary: More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in Ukraine, according to a new projection based on leaked official data, an estimate that sheds new light on the staggering cost of President Vladimir Putin’s war.
story: More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in Ukraine, according to a new projection based on leaked official data, an estimate that sheds new light on the staggering cost of President Vladimir Putin’s war.

The grim assessment comes more than 4½ years after the Kremlin’s invasion of its neighbor, an all-out war that has consumed Russian society. The death toll has been mounting with each painstaking ground assault, with no end to the conflict in sight despite pressure from President Donald Trump for Kyiv to make a deal.

The leak from Russia’s state statistics agency, Rosstat — released by Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers earlier this month — reveals that at least 490,000 Russian soldiers had been killed in Ukraine based on registered deaths as of the end of September. That’s according to breakdowns by a range of independent media, including the BBC and others, that were published this week. But one exiled Russian media outlet, Meduza, also used the leaked mortality data to project the total number of military deaths, including those that have not yet been recorded.
Meduza estimates that number to be 720,000.
NBC News did not have access to the leaked data and could not authenticate it or independently confirm these numbers.
Neither Moscow nor Kyiv provide regular updates on their battlefield losses.

Mediazona, along with the BBC Russian Service and a team of volunteers, has been compiling a separate named list of Russian war dead using open-source data for years, given the difficulty of gauging the true impact of the war on Russian society.

In its analysis, Mediazona said it arrived at the 490,000 war dead number from the 29.7 million records it obtained from the hackers that covered nearly all death registrations in Russia from early 2021 through September this year, based mainly on records with an “explicit military cause of death” and court rulings declaring people dead.

The leaked data was cross-checked against Mediazona’s own named list and matched 95% of the records, as well as the publicly accessible national Probate Registry, a database of inheritance cases, and Rosstat’s own official mortality statistics, the outlet said.

Mediazona said it also checked against possible data tempering and fake military death injections by cross-referencing a unique vital record number that every death registration carries, and court rulings, which often cite death record numbers.

“We are confident that this data is genuine,” the outlet said, adding that fabricating a dataset of this scale from scratch would be “impossible” especially as it checks out against official registries.

The hackers shared leaked data with a number of other exiled Russian media outlets and the BBC, who all arrived at a figure close to the 490,000 reported by Mediazona. A similar estimate of half a million Russian troops killed was also shared by a senior British defense official in September.

Before the new analysis of the data in the Rosstat leak, the verified named list of Russia’s war dead compiled by Mediazona and the BBC stood at just over 289,000. It was based on obituaries, local news and official registries, and was the only publicly available database containing the fallen soldiers’ names.
The Russian Defense Ministry has not officially updated its death toll in Ukraine since the early months of the war, when then-Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu said it stood at nearly 6,000.

Mediazona warned that due to a considerable lag in military death registrations, Rosstat may not yet have finished capturing deaths from 2025. “That means the leaked records through late September — however authentic and reliable they are — still fall short of the true death toll,” it said.

title: Trump proposes a new wave of tariffs on China, E.U. and other trade partners
summary: Trump proposes a new wave of tariffs on China, E.U. and other trade partners
story: The Trump administration on Wednesday proposed a new wave of tariffs on the European Union, China and other trade partners, the result of a probe into what it says are unfair manufacturing practices.

Some of the proposals include tariffs of at least 20% on China, which would match an agreement reached with the White House. But the duties could reach up to 40% if talks between the two countries fail.
The United States’ current trade truce with China was recently extended and is set to expire in January.

The tariffs will be implemented under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, a statute that the White House has relied upon more frequently for trade authority ever since the Supreme Court blocked many of Trump’s 2025 country-specific tariffs, imposed under a different authority.

Wednesday’s announcement came less than a month after Trump’s tariff policies — and the inflation they fueled — contributed to Republicans’ sweeping losses in the midterm elections. Inflation hit 3.7% in September, driven primarily by energy prices, but also by higher prices of goods.

In announcing the details of the new duties, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said that the overall rates applied to each trading partner would not surpass levels that were previously agreed to as part of bilateral framework trade deals.
“When it all nets out, it really will just top up a few percentage points,” Greer said on CNBC.
“So what we’re proposing today are actually a set of targeted tariffs to respond to this problem of excess capacity,” he added.
For example, Trump agreed to cap tariffs on E.U. imports at 15% as part of a deal reached in 2025. On Wednesday, the trade representative reiterated that cap.
The new tariffs will not stack on top of existing duties, except for the case of China.

“We’ve talked to our trading partners about this,” Greer said. “They know what we’re proposing. I think a lot of this is baked in, and I don’t think any of these would actually take effect earlier than a couple of months from now.”
He said he expects that “a broad” negotiation with trading partners would follow Wednesday’s proposals.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
But tensions continue to flare with trading partners, especially between Canada, the E.U. and China.

Overnight, a spokesperson for the Chinese Commerce Ministry rejected the basis for the new tariffs. “Tariff wars and trade wars are in the interests of neither side,” the spokesperson said in a briefing for reporters.
“So-called ‘overcapacity’ is a false proposition,” the spokesperson added. “China opposes using it as a pretext for political manipulation.”
Separately, the European Union said its members “strongly reject the premise that Europe is a source of structural overcapacity. To the contrary, Europe is among those most exposed to overcapacity.”

The bloc shares the Trump administration’s concerns about overcapacity, said Olof Gill, deputy chief spokesman for the the European Commission. Given the mutual concerns, the E.U.  regrets “the lack of joint action” with the United States to address the problem.

Just weeks ago, Greer accused the E.U. of “aggressively” supporting Airbus and said that a loan from the European Investment Bank to the French aerospace giant threatened to inject “substantial uncertainty into transatlantic trade in the aerospace sector.”
The E.U. rejected Greer’s assertion, saying the loan was normal and he had “really no grounds” to question it. The bloc, made up of 27 countries, is America’s largest trading partner.
Meanwhile, in August, trade talks with Canada collapsed after Prime Minister Mark Carney said the Trump administration requested “uneconomic” and unfair terms at the last minute.

Carney recalled his negotiators to Ottawa and for more than three months the two sides have traded verbal barbs. Canada is the country’s third-largest trading partner, according to data through September.
Recently, informal talks resumed between the U.S. and Canada but a formal deal does not yet appear to be within reach.
On Wednesday, Greer said those talks with Canada were continuing, due to some outstanding “sticking points.”
Another key U.S. trading partner, Mexico, was not included in Wednesday’s tariff proposals.

“I think the most important one where we’re still going through the investigation process, is Mexico,” Greer told CNBC. “I think it’ll be a little bit more time before we release that report,” he said.

title: Talking Shop with Tyler Cameron
summary: Tyler Cameron’s 2026 was an HGTV and DWTS whirlwind, now he’s sharing the gifts he’s getting his fiance before the year ends and all the things that’ll help him become a “hot dad” in 2027.
story: Talking Shop is our series where we talk to interesting people about their most interesting buys.

It seems impossible that Tyler Cameron could have a bigger year than 2026. In the past 12 months, he got engaged, announced that he’s expecting a baby with fiancé Tate Madden and competed on Dancing with the Stars. Plus, his HGTV show Bachelor Mansion Takeover premiered and he became part owner of Tinkr, a brand that sells modern home tools. Yet somehow, 2027 is looking just as huge. His daughter is due in March, he’s planning a wedding, he’s going on tour with Dancing with the Stars and he’s filming a new HGTV show. Before all of that, however, he’s slowing down to celebrate the holidays with his loved ones, something he’s looking forward to more than ever.

“I’m not going to lie, I was the biggest Grinch,” says Cameron. “I was never really into the holidays because there was always something happening with my family, and it was a ‘hold my breath’ period for a long time. But Tate has really gotten rid of the Grinch and brought out the best in me, so now I love the holidays and I’m so excited about them.”

Cameron’s favorite part of the holidays is decorating, especially his Christmas tree. He and Madden put theirs up on November 1 so they could start putting presents underneath it. One of Cameron’s go-to places to get gifts quickly is Amazon, a retailer he’s currently partnering with to curate collections of his top picks and keep track of ideas for everyone. Below, he shared the top gifts he’s giving and hopes to receive this year while reflecting on a jam-packed year.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
Garmin Vívoactive Smartwatch

Dancing with the Stars was a whirlwind that Cameron says gave him numerous life lessons. The biggest? “It’s about the ability to put yourself out there and be fearless,” he says. “Sometimes I get imposter syndrome, or feel like I don’t fit in or I don’t belong — I go back to being that simple guy from Jupiter [Florida] who builds houses, and I forget that I get to do some really cool stuff. During Dancing with the Stars, it was all about that mantra of ‘you can.’ You can put yourself out there and be great. You can step on stage and mess up and still come back. It was a giant confidence builder and honestly one of the most fulfilling things I’ve ever done.”

Because he was competing on DWTS, Cameron couldn’t run the 2026 New York City Marathon, which he’s done a few times. He hopes to race in 2027 and apply what he learned on the show to training. The Garmin Vívoactive Smartwatch will also be something he relies on to track his miles, energy levels, sleep and health metrics like heart rate, so that’s one of the gifts he’d love to receive.
JBL Boombox 4

“Everyone being happy and healthy is really the top thing on my personal wish list,” says Cameron. “It’s an easy thing to say, but I’ve really dialed in on health lately. I lost 11 pounds during Dancing with the Stars, so I want to continue leaning into that — 2027 is the year of being a hot dad.”

Beyond running, Cameron likes to do group workouts. When he takes his training outside, he brings the JBL Boombox with him to play music during sessions. The speaker is a gift he says any audiophile in your life would appreciate, especially if they enjoy being the DJ in their friend group.
Therabody SleepMask

“Rest is so important — I’m very big on it,” says Cameron. “After workouts I use things like a foam roller, but for sleep, I put on mouth tape and nose strips — I do all that kind of stuff. I also use the Therabody sleep mask.” It blocks light to help him fall and stay asleep, and he can choose from three vibration patterns to enhance his slumber with an eye massage. He’s gifting it to loved ones who could use some R&R.
We can help you find
Salt & Stone Body Wash

This holiday season is the last one Cameron and Madden will celebrate as a party of two — next year, they’ll be sharing their first Christmas with their daughter. So when it comes to buying his fiancé gifts this holiday season, Cameron’s goal is to make her feel totally taken care of.

“She has a baby list that I’ll start shopping from, but I want to get her things for herself and that will help her nest,” he says. “She loves anything from HydroJug, and she’s a big fan of Salt & Stone body washes and deodorants. I’m getting her all those simple things that make her happy so she can focus on herself and get ready for the baby.”
Tinkr Laser Electric Scissors

Cameron’s background is in home construction — before he was on The Bachelorette, and still to this day, he’s a contractor, as well as a real estate agent. He’s always working on something related to home improvement, like his new HGTV show, Let’s Go Back to Your Place, which he starts filming next week.

“The best way to describe it is if Room Raiders and House Hunters had a baby,” says Cameron. “I take a bachelor or bachelorette, and I’m their wingman. We go look at houses and they choose someone to date based on that. They never get to meet them until after they decide on the house. Just imagine if you could go through someone’s house before you go on a date with them — imagine how much you could already know about them.”

Cameron and Madden are also part owners of Tinkr, a brand that sells modern home tools. It rolled out in major retailers like Target and Kohl’s this year, and in 2027, the company is growing even more, in addition to launching new products. Cameron says he loves Tinkr’s jump starter and toolbox, while Madden is obsessed with the electric scissors. “They’re a must-have in our house for breaking down boxes,” he says.
Why trust NBC Selected?

I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who leads our Talking Shop series, interviewing people like Paris Hilton, Maureen Kelly, Lindsay Hubbard and Chase Crawford. To write this article, I talked to Tyler Cameron about his experience on Dancing with the Stars, his upcoming HGTV show and his top Amazon holiday gift picks.

title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia lands in Spain a ‘free man’ after deportation battle
summary: Kilmar Abrego Garcia is in Spain after voluntarily leaving the United States on Tuesday, ending a closely watched and controversial deportation battle that became a symbol for the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown.
story: Kilmar Abrego Garcia is in Spain after voluntarily leaving the United States on Tuesday, ending a closely watched and controversial deportation battle that became a symbol for the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown.
Abrego Garcia was ordered by a federal judge to leave the United States by Tuesday, a U.S. official confirmed to NBC News.
Speaking at a virtual press conference from Spain on Wednesday afternoon, Abrego Garcia said, “I am happy and I am celebrating my freedom.”

“I feel free from everything bad that I have been through, and now I can breathe in freedom,” Abrego Garcia said in Spanish. “God has given me the understanding and the strength throughout this entire process because in the beginning I was afraid. But now, I am not afraid to confront — just as I have already confronted — a government.”
Abrego Garcia was first spotted Tuesday night boarding a commercial flight at Washington Dulles International Airport bound for Madrid.
Flight tracking data indicated his plane landed in the Spanish capital of Madrid early Wednesday.

Abrego Garcia, wearing a dark hooded jacket, was seen at the Washington airport with his wife and brother, as well as lawyer Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg, and representatives from immigrant rights group We Are CASA (Central American Solidarity and Assistance).
CASA said in a news release Tuesday that Abrego Garcia is also “planning on hosting various international speaking engagements, with stops planned in different countries.”

Before he boarded the flight, Sandoval-Moshenberg said his client was leaving the country his way instead of the way the administration wanted “in shackles” as an Immigration and Customs Enforcement detainee headed on a government plane to the West African country of Liberia.
Abrego Garcia would return to the United States to open arms and the reunification of his family here following the end of Donald Trump’s presidential term, the attorney said.
His client “has many options to return to the United States as the husband of a U.S. citizen and the father of a U.S. citizen child,” he added.
He added, “Where he goes from here, where he chooses to settle for the next two years while he waits out the end of this administration, will be his choice.”
The Salvadoran national became a central figure in the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown last year after he was mistakenly deported to his home country.
Abrego Garcia said on Wednesday that this time he left the United States with his freedom, “not like before when they took me out inhumanely.”

White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis late Tuesday hailed his departure as a win. “The El Salvadoran man chose to self-deport to Spain — a country that has been wrecked by open border policies. Good riddance,” she said.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin used similar language, calling this a matter of self-deportation, and characterized his presence in the United States as focused on an alleged life of crime.
“We are delighted to announce that Kilmar Abrego Garcia has self-deported,” he said. “Now, this El Salvadoran man cannot terrorize innocent Americans.”

Court records in Maryland show that Abrego Garcia voluntarily agreed to leave the U.S. under an agreement with federal authorities who had sought his removal. The agreement, it said, would end those proceedings.
The 31-year-old man immigrated to the U.S. illegally as a teenager, but has been in the U.S. for years, is married to an American and has a child with her.
He had lived and worked in Maryland for years under regular ICE supervision.
In 2019, an immigration judge ruled that he could not be deported to El Salvador because he faced danger there from gang members.

He was deported there anyway in 2025 and sent to the Central American country’s CECOT megaprison. Activists have decried alleged abuses there and described inmates being packed into cells with no time outdoors.
Prison officials allowed Abrego Garcia a brief outside meeting with Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Maryland, who told reporters that Abrego Garcia had “experienced trauma” after an “illegal abduction.”
On Wednesday at the virtual press conference, Van Hollen described that actions of the Trump administration against Abrego Garcia as “a vendetta” because he “stood up for his constitutional rights.”
“Kilmar and his family are relieved that he is now in a place of his choosing, a free man and living with dignity,” Van Hollen said.
After Abrego Garcia was returned to the U.S. from El Salvador, ICE officials admitted in court filings that his deportation had been an “administrative error.”

But shortly after his return, Abrego Garcia was charged with human smuggling in a case stemming from a 2022 traffic stop for alleged speeding in Tennessee in which he was driving a van with multiple immigrant passengers.

Abrego Garcia told Tennessee Highway Patrol troopers he was taking the group of nine to a construction job. Authorities there did not pursue charges. A federal judge dismissed the 2025 Department of Justice case, saying the Trump administration failed to rebut the “presumption of vindictiveness.” The government appealed.
The administration continued to pursue Abrego Garcia’s removal, and he was fighting that in a lawsuit that was ongoing prior to today’s news.
Abrego Garcia has been fighting deportation to Liberia, as proposed by Department of Homeland Security officials. He wanted to go to Costa Rica, according to court records.
Trump and immigration officials alleged Abrego Garcia was an MS-13 gang member, something he denied.
In 2019 records from a loitering case in which he was picked up in a Home Depot parking lot, authorities in Prince George’s County said that Abrego appeared to be an MS-13 member.

They said they made that conclusion based on his clothing (including a Chicago Bulls hat) and tattoos, as well as a proven confidential informant. Abrego Garcia was not formally arrested that day, police said, and they did not have contact with him again. Abrego Garcia’s lawyers later called the evidence of his gang membership “hearsay.”

U.S. District Judge Waverly Crenshaw, who presided over the Tennessee smuggling case, warned top Trump administration officials to stop making statements about Abrego Garcia that were “exaggerated if not simply inaccurate” and could influence a potential jury.

title: Family of teen killed by Georgia police officer demands release of body camera footage
summary: The family of a Black teenager in Georgia who was killed in a police shooting said Tuesday that it wants transparency and called on the police department to release the officer body camera footage.
story: The family of a Black teenager in Georgia who was killed in a police shooting said Tuesday that it wants transparency and called on the police department to release the officer body camera footage.

The 16-year-old, identified by the family and its attorneys as Tyrie Howse, was shot and killed Nov. 3 following an encounter with a Henry County police officer outside a Krispy Kreme in Stockbridge, about 21 miles southeast of Atlanta.

Howse’s mother said Tuesday at a news conference that her son had left his cellphone somewhere the night before and went to get it. She was a few minutes from picking him up from the Krispy Kreme parking lot when he was shot, she said.
“There was no reason, no reason at all for this to happen to him,” Taneshia Puckett said.

Preliminary information released by the Georgia Bureau of Investigation said a Henry County police officer approached Howse and a 17-year-old in the parking lot of a Krispy Kreme, a news release states.

The officer briefly spoke with the teens “before giving verbal commands for the 17-year-old to take his hands out of his pockets,” the release says. Authorities have not said what prompted the officer to approach the teens.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The GBI said the 17-year-old “passed a handgun” to Howse, who allegedly ran away from the area with the gun, according to the release.

“The 16-year-old did not drop the gun, and the officer shot at the 16-year-old, hitting him. Medical aid was provided to the 16-year-old. The 16-year-old was pronounced deceased on scene,” the GBI said.

No officers were injured, and a firearm was recovered from the scene, according to the GBI. The officer involved in the shooting was placed on administrative leave pending the conclusion of the investigation, police said.

Attorneys Ben Crump and Harry Daniels, who are representing Howse’s family, said they have viewed witness video showing the aftermath of the shooting and cannot see a firearm in the video they viewed. They called on officials to release the body camera footage.
“There’s nothing stopping this Henry County Police Department or this Henry County district attorney from being transparent and showing the video,” Crump said at the news conference.
He said Howse, a junior at Woodland High School, was an honor roll student who dreamed of becoming a pediatric nurse.
“I fail to understand why the most dangerous thing in America to police seems to be young Black people running away from them,” he said.

The Henry County Police Department said in a Nov. 10 statement that it asked the GBI to investigate the shooting and that it was aware of calls to release the body camera footage and other evidence, but “any potential release must be evaluated in coordination with the appropriate investigative and legal authorities.”
The department did not immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday.
The GBI said the investigative case file will be turned over to the Henry County District Attorney’s Office for review once completed.
The district attorney’s office said in a Nov. 19 statement that it had not yet received the case file and was not in possession of the body camera footage.

“Once the GBI completes its investigation and submits its findings, our office will conduct a thorough and independent review of the entire case file to determine whether criminal charges are warranted,” the district attorney’s office said. “Our decision will be guided solely by the facts, the evidence, and the applicable law.”

title: Judge denies bail for former Penn State fraternity brother at center of drug bust
summary: A federal judge on Tuesday denied bail to the former Penn State student authorities say was at the center of a drug trafficking ring at the university, ordering him to remain in custody pending trial.
story: A federal judge on Tuesday denied bail to the former Penn State student authorities say was at the center of a drug trafficking ring at the university, ordering him to remain in custody pending trial.
Agostino Abbatiello, 24, of Westbury, New York, was arrested and charged with one count of conspiracy to distribute cocaine and six counts of distributing cocaine earlier this month.

Federal prosecutors accused Abbatiello, a former member of Sigma Chi, of conspiring to sell at least five kilograms of cocaine between January 2023 and December 2024 in State College, Pennsylvania, according to an indictment.
Abbatiello’s conspiracy charge carries a minimum of 10 years in prison and a maximum of life. He has pleaded not guilty to all of the charges.

“The court’s decision to deny bail is incredibly disappointing, and in our view, fundamentally wrong,” Abbatiello’s lawyer, Edward J. Rymsza, said in an email. “We vigorously disagree with the ruling and will be appealing.”
Federal prosecutors filed a motion on Wednesday in support of Abbatiello’s detention. Officials argued Abbatiello poses a danger to the community and is a flight risk.

The Justice Department also argued that the “weight of the evidence” warrants his detention, noting that investigators “utilized cooperating witnesses, controlled drug purchases, search warrants, and interviews to dismantle this drug trafficking organization.”
“The evidence continues to grow stronger,” the motion reads.

On Sunday, Abbatiello’s attorney filed a brief opposing Abbatiello’s detention. The attorney, Edward J. Rymsza, argued that Abbatiello “has already demonstrated” he will “appear and obey the law while on release.”

State officials arrested and charged Abbatiello in connection with the same alleged drug trafficking scheme in August. In the state case, Abbatiello was charged with felony corrupt organizations, conspiracy and dealing in proceeds of unlawful activity.
Rymsza said his client voluntarily surrendered to state authorities, has appeared at scheduled court proceedings, and has been out on $250,000 bail without violating it.
According to the brief in opposition, Abbatiello had been living with his parents and siblings at their home on Long Island, New York.

Thirteen other people were arrested and charged by state officials in connection with the alleged drug ring. The other defendants include current and former students and the father of a former student, and they face various counts.

Penn State announced that it will no longer recognize the other fraternity officials said was involved in the alleged drug ring, Delta Upsilon, hours after the DOJ announced Abbatiello’s charges. Sigma Chi already lost its recognition.

title: I’m a Divorce Lawyer Who Watched ‘War.’ Here’s Who Really Came Out on Top
summary: Divorce lawyer Hannah Hembree Bell reacts to the “War” finale and says who came out on top and who won in the end.
story: “Take it From Me” is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this edition, a divorce lawyer breaks down the “War” finale.
Hannah Hembree Bell couldn’t turn her brain off while watching “War.”

A divorce lawyer and owner of her own Texas family law firm, Bell guides clients through situations resembling the characters’. In her assessment, the two leads were “awesome” — but the “legal part (of the show) was patently ridiculous.”
“War” follows a billionaire tech founder (Dominic West) and a Hollywood actor’s high-profile, high-net-worth split, and all the legal wheelings and dealings that ensue.

While watching, she was struck by how differently she would have advised Morgan and Carla than their own legal advisors. The lawyers brazenly blew past any attempt at a settlement, and employed shocking (and illegal) tactics like placing a mole in the other firm’s team.

“The lawyers inflamed the conflict. That’s why you have to be really careful in picking your lawyers. Are you picking lawyers who have big egos? Are they known to be willing to burn everything down, including your life?” she says.
Still, as over-the-top as the antics were, the “War” finale, which aired on Nov. 18, offered up a lesson or two for anyone going through a divorce.
What Happens at the End of ‘War’, and Who Wins?
After all that — and there is a lot of “that” — Carla and Morgan come to a reasonable settlement, bypassing the lawyers’ interventions.
They agree for Morgan to give Carla 50 percent of shares and monthly payments until he retires. They also have joint access to Carla’s son Gabriel (Aran Murphy), who Morgan helped raise.
Rather than Carla vs. Morgan, the show ended up becoming Carla and Morgan vs. their lawyers, and their lawyers’ scorched earth tactics.
“Ultimately, the winners are Carla, Morgan and Gabe because they came to terms that was best for their family given their unique situations,” Bell says.
The Advice She Would’ve Given Carla and Morgan
At the start of the divorce process, Bell advises her clients to dream up their best-case scenario.
Then, during each step, she has her clients ask themselves, “Will this action get me closer to or farther away from where I’m trying to go?”
Bell says most of the show would have been avoided if Morgan and Carla had taken that advice. “They would have just had a coffee and worked out the deal,” she says.

Morgan, for example, would have wanted a relationship with Carla’s son Gabe and control over Zephyr, his business. Carla would have wanted a good relationship with Gabe, too, and compensation for the work she did for building Zephyr.

“Then I would have said, ‘OK, if that’s the goal, and especially the Gabe part, we’re not going to go serving people at their movie premiere. We’re not going to go setting honey pots. That does not advance your interest,” she says.
“But if they’re not clear on what their interests are and what the outcome they want is, then they can take actions that thwart their plan.”
The 2 Lessons ‘War’ Offers About Divorce
“War” offers up other cautionary tales, including what happens when people act emotionally. Bell advises her clients to “do nothing when activated.”
“Whether you’re super happy, super sad, super mad, wait until that emotion passes before you act or do anything,” she says.
Her other recommendation is to “keep a tether to the person you’re divorcing, if it’s at all possible” — though, of course, sometimes it’s not.

Caught up in the drama and defensive measures, Carla and Morgan lost their connection to each other. But it got reestablished when Morgan’s love letter was read in open court, and they landed on a fair deal.
“If they had kept that connection, even if it was strained, I think they could have gotten there a lot sooner,” she says.

title: Could the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade 2026 Be Canceled? Macy’s Shares Statement
summary: Heavy rain and wind is expected for Thanksgiving Day. Here’s what that could mean for the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade in New York City.
story: Snoopy, Bluey and SpongeBob will still make their appearance in the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade — just a bit later than expected.

Heavy rain and high winds are predicted in the Northeast on Thanksgiving Day, which raised the question of whether the 100th edition of the annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City would be grounded or canceled.
In a statement shared on Nov. 25, Macy’s confirmed it would be postponing the parade to Saturday, Nov. 28.

“The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration. Due to the expected severe weather, the 100th March of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will move to Saturday, Nov. 28. Our team is working through the operational logistics for this change and will share details as they are finalized. We expect the Parade to kick off at 8:30 a.m. on Saturday,” the statement read.

The parade is broadcast live on NBC, Peacock and Telemundo. NBC also issued a statement: “Due to the extreme weather conditions, the city of New York, Macy’s and NBC have decided, in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators, to move the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov. 28. More details to follow. In addition, NBC will telecast the 2025 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade tomorrow at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones.”
A record-setting 100 balloons were set to float down the streets of Manhattan on Thursday, hosted by TODAY’s Savannah Guthrie, Al Roker and Hoda Kotb.
Here’s what to know as far as the forecast and change to the parade schedule.
Weather Forecast for Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade 2027

Heavy rain and wind gusts of 50-60 miles per hour, with the strongest winds from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., are forecast for New York City on Thanksgiving, according to NYC Emergency Management. There is a high wind watch for the New York City metro area from 10 a.m. Thursday to 1 a.m. Friday.
About 1-2 inches of rain, up to 2.75 inches, are also expected, with some flash flooding and possible thunderstorms.
“In the 32 years I’ve been doing the parade, I’ve never seen a forecast like this,” weatherman Al Roker said on TODAY on Nov. 25.
New York City regulations stipulate the balloons must be grounded if sustained winds exceed 23 miles per hour and gusts exceed 34 miles per hour.

Those regulations were put in place in 1998 after severe weather at the previous year’s parade, which had wind gusts up to 43 mph. The wind sent a Dr. Seuss Cat in the Hat balloon careening into a lamppost on 72nd Street and Central Park West, snapping off a metal arm and injuring four people.
NYPD officers also had to ground and deflate the Barney and Pink Panther balloons, according to The Weather Channel.
As a result, the parade will take place on Saturday, Nov. 28.
What Happens in Bad Weather?
There has only been one edition of the parade where there were no inflatables flying. Fierce winds and rain prompted parade organizers to ground all the balloons at the 1971 event.
The NYPD and parade organizers can adjust how high the balloons are flying instead of grounding them entirely in the case of windy conditions.
At the 2019 parade, wind gusts went right up to the edge of the limit, reaching 33 mph. Vehicles were anchored to the balloons to fly them lower down Sixth Avenue in Manhattan.

Otherwise, the show has typically gone on despite the conditions. In 1989, 4.4 inches of snow fell by noon in the snowiest parade on record, according to The Weather Channel. In 2006, parade-goers endured nearly two inches of rain.
The 2018 celebration brought frigid temperatures of 17 degrees with 20-mph winds. A bundled-up Al reported on TODAY that it was the coldest Macy’s parade in history.
Has the Parade Ever Been Canceled?
Yes, but not for weather.
The parade, which began in 1924, was not held between 1942 and 1944 due to World War II.
The show has gone on through heavy rain, blanketing snow, bone-chilling temperatures and strong winds — but never canceled for inclement weather.

The giant balloons were first introduced in 1927 with Felix the Cat. Parade organizers used to release all the balloons into the sky at the end of the parade until a 40-foot flying blue hippo balloon released at the 1931 parade sailed off in the sky and was never found.

title: Miley Cyrus Wore a ‘Very Classic Bridal Look’ to Her Wedding, but Added a Bit of ‘Rock and Roll’, Dress Designer Says
summary: Miley Cyrus’ wedding dress analyzed by Hayley Paige. Here’s what she thinks of the Saint Laurent look.
story: Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando are officially married. The “Flowers” singer married Morando, a drummer, in a ceremony at Frank Sinatra’s Palm Springs estate over the weekend.
For the nuptials, Cyrus wore a long-sleeved, high-neck Saint Laurent gown, which she showed off in a series of photos shared on Instagram.
Wedding dress designer Hayley Paige calls the dress “streamlined, sensual and a little cinematic” in an email statement to TODAY.com.
Her favorite feature is the “juxtaposition of the more demure front with the dramatic open back.”
Paige also points out how the dress is in conversation with the accessories and makeup for an aesthetic that screams, well, Miley.
“I also really enjoy the contrast of the smoky eye and the diamonds against such a clean silhouette,” Paige says. There’s a little rock-and-roll sprinkled into an otherwise very classic bridal look.”
The guests, according to photos, all wore black, which created a “striking backdrop” for her gown. “It’s a sartorial choice that lends itself to some really beautiful, editorial imagery,” she said.
The ceremony marks Cyrus’ second wedding. She was previously married to actor Liam Hemsworth from 2018 to 2020. For her December 2018 nuptials, Cyrus wore an ivory corseted Vivienne Westwood gown.
Cyrus’ recent wedding dress, Paige said, has a “more fluid, elongated silhouette” than the first one.

But there are similarities — namely, in their shared used of drape and their simplicity. “Both dresses rely heavily on the beauty of the fabric and how it interacts with the body, rather than surface embellishment,” Paige said.
For Paige, Cyrus’ dress shows a trend in current bridal fashion, which is that both minimalism and maximalism are having a moment.

“I think that speaks to how much more individualistic bridal fashion has become. There is less of a prescribed aesthetic for what a bride should look like, which gives brides more creative agency and us as designers a lot more room to play,” Piage said.
Cyrus and Morando got engaged last December. He proposed with a cushion cut diamond set in a chunky gold band.
The pair then hinted at their impending wedding in September when they appeared together in Cyrus’ steamy music video for song “Let’s Get Married.”

title: Jenna Bush Hager Turned 45 on TODAY, and She Almost Instantly Started Crying: ‘I Love My Life’
summary: Jenna Bush Hager got emotional on her 45th birthday as Sheinelle Jones celebrated with custom pajamas and video messages from famous friends.
story: The Nov. 25 episode of TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle was all about Jenna Bush Hager’s 45th birthday, and it took her about a minute to start crying.
“Forty-five is a notch in the belt,” Sheinelle Jones said. “How do you feel?”
“I feel 26,” Jenna said. Then her voice caught.
“I mean, I feel young, and yet here I am,” she said, tearing up. “But also, why? Why do I … this happens every birthday.”
She kept going anyway.
“I do feel really fulfilled, and I know that that’s such a lucky thing, to really love my life,” she said.
“That is the most beautiful thing,” Sheinelle said. “That’s all you could want as a parent, is to hear your kids say that they love their life.”

Still crying, Jenna turned to her co-host. “I love my life. I love sitting next to you every day,” she said. “We’ve had almost a year of shows together. I love going home to my kids and my husband and my cats.”
Then she thanked the crew.

“I wake up every morning excited to be with every single one of the people in this room, and I know not everybody gets that life,” she said. “So I hope that I’m going to take every day of this year and feel really grateful.”
Sheinelle’s gift was a pair of custom pajamas printed with photos of the two co-hosts and Jenna’s cats.
“I just want to be with you always,” Sheinelle said.
Jenna shares her birthday with her twin sister, Barbara Pierce Bush. The two celebrated early this year because they’re traveling for Thanksgiving.

“We went out for a dinner, just the two of us, and somebody brought us a little cake, and we took a selfie because there was nobody to take the picture,” Jenna said. “We try to celebrate in some way, and when we were young, we definitely celebrated.”
Sheinelle has twins too: Clara and Uche, 14, a girl and a boy. She said this could be the first year the ninth graders want separate parties.
Jenna never felt that pull. “We shared, and I was happy to share with her,” she said, explaining that she and Barbara “kind of shared a group” of friends.
Celebrity friends sent video messages too, including Andy Cohen, Leslie Bibb, Ciara and Russell Wilson, Chelsea Handler, Dwyane Wade, Aaron Paul and Bryan Cranston.
Olivia Munn knew what to expect.

“Gosh, you are one of my most favorite people in the entire world. You are so much fun. You are such a great mom,” Munn said. “Are you crying yet? I mean, if you’re not crying right now, I kind of feel insulted, because you kind of cry about everything.”

title: Teri Polo Reveals the Acting Advice Robert De Niro Gave Her on the Set of ‘Meet the Parents’
summary: Teri Polo, aka “Pamcakes” from “Meet the Parents,” opens up on filming the latest sequel, “Focker-In-Law,” and the advice she got from Robert De Niro.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Commercial Break,” TODAY.com catches up with guests between takes in Studio 1A for unfiltered moments and more questions.
Teri Polo’s pants aren’t very comfortable. Like, not even a little. After noticing her shifting around, I ask if I can grab her different chair for our conversation.
“No, no, no. It’s these pants. I didn’t practice sitting in these,” she says of her stylish grey slacks with a laugh.

Down to earth and generous with her smile, Polo settles in, awkward pants and all, to talk “Focker-In-Law,” the latest installment in the “Meet the Parents” franchise, dropping in theaters on Nov. 25.

The classic 2000 movie is what cemented Polo’s acting career, and in the 25 years since its release, she’s steadily worked in a variety of television and film projects, including two other “Meet the Parents” sequels: “Meet the Fockers” and “Little Fockers.”

According to Polo, being recruited for this most recent film, which also stars Ben Stiller, Robert De Niro and newcomer Ariana Grande, left her “speechless.” More than that, she cried when she got the call.

Polo tells  TODAY.com for “Commercial Break” what specifically brought the actor to tears, which of her “Focker-In-Law” co-stars is among the “kindest people in the world” and the advice “Bob” De Niro gave her on the set that she’ll never forget.
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.
It’s so funny that you asked that because I say that all the time: When we were filming, it was, “Oh, we’re funny” and “Oh, that was great.” But we had no clue. We had no idea.

You had Robert De Niro and you had Ben Stiller, who was at the height of his rise, if you will, of comedy. So, yes, of course, it was going to do well. But the first weekend, it was No. 1. We were like, “OK, wow. this is great. That’s amazing.”
The second weekend it was No. 1 and they were like, “Holy you-know.” And the third weekend was beyond. And I knew they were like, “OK, we’ve got to get to work right on the second one!”

But we had no idea. We truly didn’t. We just worked hard on the movie and spent three months working away and having fun. And I knew. I was like, “This is never, ever, ever going to happen in my life again, so I’m not going to take one single moment for granted.” And I just had the best time filming that.

It was, for us, kind of just sliding right back into the roles. It wasn’t the same in the sense that we’re obviously far older now. We’re 26, 27, years older now. It’s not that it was easier, but there was an ease to it that we just went right back into our characters. I liken it to a nice warm hug.

And then you’ve got Ariana, Skyler (Gisondo), Eduardo (Franco) and Beanie (Feldstein) coming in and just putting this insane life to it that’s going to bring in a whole new generation. A generation that doesn’t even have to go back and watch the first one because one can live on its own to be perfectly honest.

It parallels the first one so much and the younger generation is going to experience this one for the first time, like the generations back in 2000 experienced “Meet the Parents.” So it’s a brand new experience for some people, and just a complete and utter nostalgic experience for us old folkies.
It’s more than satisfying. It’s like, I could retire now and be like, “I hit it, man. I hit it,” you know?

When they called me to do the fourth one, I was literally speechless — and I’m never speechless. My agent and manager were on the phone going, “Teri, Teri, are you there?” And I’m sitting there speechless, crying.
The last thing that would’ve ever entered my mind to do for them was a fourth one. And now ...
It’s not confirmed at all. I mean, they leave it very, very open-ended. The last line of the movie is very interesting, shall we say. But I literally have no idea. I’m keeping my fingers crossed.
No. Because I think I’m so used to it. (Owen) is very much like that in real life, too. He’s so dry. He’s so genuine. He’s just so real that when he delivers his lines.
That was something I learned from Bob (De Niro) from the very first one. I was like, “I’m never going to have this experience again, I’m going to learn all I can from (De Niro).”

And I asked him, “What’s the difference between comedy and drama?” I’m paraphrasing, but he basically said: “It is the honesty and genuineness with which you deliver the line that will make it dramatic, make you go, ‘Oh my God.’ Or, that makes it comedic.”
Because in the first one — “I have nipples, Greg. Can you milk me?” — he meant that.
It wasn’t that he was innocent, but you hear him say and ask questions sometimes that he’s genuinely wanting to get this information.

And you see the comedy. Eduardo and Beanie and Ben, obviously, you know, everybody really means what they’re saying and you’re laughing your butt off. So with Owen, he just really means it. So, it wasn’t difficult at all. Plus, he’s one of the sweetest, kindest people in the world.
